fix(browser-tools): the skill described the tool from before RFC-01 Phase 5

The deployed skill is what an agent reads before it ever runs `bt guide`,
and it described a surface that has not existed since Phase 5. Not as
history, as live instruction.

What was wrong:

- A whole "Optional MCP front" section said the daemon "remains available"
  and named `mcp_daemon.py`, `mcp_broker.py` and `daemon_supervisor.py`.
  All deleted. The frontmatter description advertised it too, so it was in
  the summary an agent sees when deciding whether to load the skill.
- The verb set gave `screencast start` and `screencast stop`. Those were
  replaced by one bounded capture; running either now exits with a usage
  error.
- It said `click` and `fill` "take a fresh snapshot first". Phase 5d
  removed exactly that, and the UID rule changed with it.
- It mapped verbs to internal tool names (`list_frames`, `select_frame`,
  `take_snapshot`, `inspect_blocked`) that no caller can reach.
- `profile` was missing from the verb list entirely, along with
  `--endpoint`, the v6 UID rule, `bt --version` and
  `browser-tools-profiler`.

What replaces it:

- The UID rule as one rule: valid until the page navigates, nothing else
  invalidates it, so a snapshot between two fills is unnecessary.
- `screencast` as the single bounded capture, with why there is no stop.
- `profile list` / `delete` / `migrate`, and `--endpoint URL`.
- A "What does not carry between invocations" section: page state stays,
  session state does not, and the four things agents reach for that are
  session state, each with the error the browser returns. This is where
  the file-upload recipe via a UID's `backendNodeId` lives, and the
  warning that a JavaScript dialog cannot be handled at all across
  invocations.
- A CPU profiling section for the second console script.
- `bt --version` up front, and a pointer saying `bt guide` is the
  authority, since a test fails the build when the guide drifts and
  nothing enforces this document.

The verb list is verified against `cli.build_parser()`: no verb in the
parser is missing here, and nothing here is absent from the parser. Every
documented command was run against the installed build.

`bt --version` ships in browser-tools 0.5.0.
EOF

All done. Eight PRs, each merged after CI, then released as 0.5.0.

| PR | What |
|---|---|
| [#118](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/118) | RFC-01 v7: every phase landed, with the PR behind each step |
| [#119](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/119) | **RFC-03 Accepted** |
| [#120](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/120) | CONTEXT.md gains the CPU Profiler |
| [#121](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/121) | CI matrix 3.13 + 3.14 |
| [#122](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/122) | Live Camoufox launch test |
| [#123](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/123) | `bt --version` |
| [#124](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/124) | Stale CHANGELOG retired |
| [#125](https://github.com/dungle-scrubs/browser-tools/pull/125) | Release 0.5.0 |

## Design

### The verb

```
run [INSTANCE] FILE [--timeout SECONDS] [--endpoint URL]
run [INSTANCE] -    [--timeout SECONDS] [--endpoint URL]
```

`FILE` is a Step List on disk. `-` reads the Step List from stdin. Exactly one
source MUST be given; giving neither, or both, is a usage error (exit 2).

Both sources are REQUIRED. A file is reviewable, diffable, and re-runnable, which
is what a flow you keep and re-run needs. stdin is what a caller that generates a flow
and does not want a temporary file needs, and some agent harnesses cannot easily
write one.

The verb is named `run` and not `script`. "Script" tells a caller it may write code,
and Design, "The execution model", specifies that it may not. Kevin settled the name on 2026-09-21; see
Decisions, item 2.

### One CDPRuntime for the run

**A Step Run MUST hold exactly one CDPRuntime for its whole duration, and every
step MUST execute over that runtime's session.** A run that opened a fresh session
per step would carry almost none of the saving, which is to say it would be ten
invocations with one command line.

Version 2 stated that requirement and stopped there. It is not enough, because two
different session mechanisms exist today and they are not interchangeable. This
section specifies the one a run uses, and what happens to the session state a step
leaves behind.

#### The connection model is the One-Shot Session's, not the handler's

Today `snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `wait-idle`, `wait-stable`, `detect`, `frames`,
`storage` and `screencast` run over a `CDPHandler`, which opens a **page-level**
WebSocket (`cdp_handler.py:404-409`, through `resolve_page_ws_url_async`) and
sends with no `sessionId` (`cdp_handler.py:411-413`). `passthrough`, `wait`,
`console-list`, `network-list` and `screenshot` open a One-Shot Session, which is a
**browser-level** connection plus `Target.attachToTarget` with `flatten: true`, and
every send and every event carries a `sessionId` (`one_shot.py:79-108`).

That difference is not cosmetic. `cdp_client.py:158-161` dispatches an event to a
handler only when the handler's `filter_session` is `None` or equal to the event's
`sessionId`. On a page-level connection there is no `sessionId`, so an event's is
`None`, and a handler registered with one never fires. `wait` registers with one
(`events.py:344`). Routing `wait`, `console-list` and `network-list` through a
page-level handler would therefore break their event delivery outright, not subtly.

So the requirement is specific:
=== does it still say no phasing? ===
408:  contract. It specifies no phasing for meeting it.

parts.text:
So the requirement is specific:

- **A Step Run MUST open one browser-level CDP connection and attach one flattened
  `Target` session, the One-Shot Session's model.** Every step sends over that
  session and every step's event handlers are registered against its `sessionId`.
- **The run's CDPRuntime, and therefore its frame manager, MUST be built over that
  attached session** rather than over a page-level WebSocket. This is a change to
  how `CDPHandler` connects today, and the RFC states it as a requirement on the
  contract. It specifies no phasing for meeting it.

#### Domain-enable state, and why it needs a rule

CDP domain enables are session state. Nothing in the tree ever sends
`Domain.disable`. Today that is harmless: the session is detached when the
invocation ends, so every enable dies with it. In a Step Run the session outlives
every step, so an enable from step 3 is still in force at step 9.

That is not merely untidy. It changes what a verb observes, and the difference was
measured rather than reasoned about:

| Case | `Runtime.enable` | `executionContextCreated` delivered |

parts.text:
Almost everything I flagged last time is done. Here is what is actually left.

## The only substantial item: build RFC-03

It is Accepted and unbuilt. Nothing else is outstanding — zero open issues, zero open PRs, both live RFCs Accepted, docs current, three machines synced.

But it has no build plan, and that is deliberate: the original brief said the RFC names no implementation work beyond the specification. So the next step is not "start coding `run`" — it is deciding the phasing.

## The one thing that needs a decision first

The RFC's hardest requirement says so itself, at line 408:

> The run's CDPRuntime, and therefore its frame manager, MUST be built over that attached session rather than over a page-level WebSocket. This is a change to how `CDPHandler` connects today, and the RFC states it as a requirement on the contract. **It specifies no phasing for meeting it.**

Two incompatible session mechanisms exist. `CDPHandler` opens a page-level socket and sends with no `sessionId`; the One-Shot Session is browser-level with `Target.attachToTarget` and a `sessionId` on every send and event. They are not interchangeable — `cdp_client.py:158-161` drops an event when the handler's `filter_session` does not match, so routing `wait` through a page-level handler breaks event delivery outright.

Converging them touches nine verbs: `snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `wait-idle`, `wait-stable`, `detect`, `frames`, `storage`, `screencast`.

## How I would phase it

I would **not** start with the verb. Start with the risk, which is also independently valuable.

1. **Converge the connection model.** Move `CDPHandler` onto the browser-level attached session. No new verb. Gate: all nine verbs behave identically, full suite green, per-invocation cost not regressed against the numbers already in `docs/rfc/03_*.measurements.md`.
2. **Parse and validate a Step List.** Reuse the `argparse` parsers *and* the `_run` semantic checks, with the `SystemExit`/stderr interception. No execution. Gate: a malformed list exits 2 with nothing sent.
3. **Execute, and the Run Document.** Failure semantics, timeouts, the composable envelope. Gate: the measured saving is realised, and step 7 of 10 failing produces the specified document and exit code.
4. **Session hygiene.** The domain enable/disable rule with the `Page`/`Runtime` exemption, frame selection across steps, the frame-manager no-match clear.
5. **Land the contract.** The normative `GUIDE.txt` entry, `Step Run` and `Step List` into `CONTEXT.md`, and the two RFC-01 amendments written into RFC-01.

Phase 1 is the one that can go wrong quietly, so it deserves its own PR and its own review before anything depends on it.

## Smaller, if you want them

- **`bt --version` should probably be in the skill's own verb block**, not only in prose. Minor.
- **`test_e2e_camoufox.py` tests a deleted surface.** It exercises `CamoufoxSession.call_tool` with MCP-era tool names. It passes and costs a second, but it is an oracle for a parity baseline, not the product. Worth asking whether it still earns its place now that a real launch is covered.

## What I would do

Phase 1, as its own PR, with a cross-family review before it merges. Say the word and I will start; the phasing above is my recommendation, not a decision I have made for you.

Almost everything I flagged last time is done. Here is what is actually left.

## The only substantial item: build RFC-03

It is Accepted and unbuilt. Nothing else is outstanding — zero open issues, zero open PRs, both live RFCs Accepted, docs current, three machines synced.

But it has no build plan, and that is deliberate: the original brief said the RFC names no implementation work beyond the specification. So the next step is not "start coding `run`" — it is deciding the phasing.

## The one thing that needs a decision first

The RFC's hardest requirement says so itself, at line 408:

> The run's CDPRuntime, and therefore its frame manager, MUST be built over that attached session rather than over a page-level WebSocket. This is a change to how `CDPHandler` connects today, and the RFC states it as a requirement on the contract. **It specifies no phasing for meeting it.**

Two incompatible session mechanisms exist. `CDPHandler` opens a page-level socket and sends with no `sessionId`; the One-Shot Session is browser-level with `Target.attachToTarget` and a `sessionId` on every send and event. They are not interchangeable — `cdp_client.py:158-161` drops an event when the handler's `filter_session` does not match, so routing `wait` through a page-level handler breaks event delivery outright.

Converging them touches nine verbs: `snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `wait-idle`, `wait-stable`, `detect`, `frames`, `storage`, `screencast`.

## How I would phase it

I would **not** start with the verb. Start with the risk, which is also independently valuable.

1. **Converge the connection model.** Move `CDPHandler` onto the browser-level attached session. No new verb. Gate: all nine verbs behave identically, full suite green, per-invocation cost not regressed against the numbers already in `docs/rfc/03_*.measurements.md`.
2. **Parse and validate a Step List.** Reuse the `argparse` parsers *and* the `_run` semantic checks, with the `SystemExit`/stderr interception. No execution. Gate: a malformed list exits 2 with nothing sent.
3. **Execute, and the Run Document.** Failure semantics, timeouts, the composable envelope. Gate: the measured saving is realised, and step 7 of 10 failing produces the specified document and exit code.
4. **Session hygiene.** The domain enable/disable rule with the `Page`/`Runtime` exemption, frame selection across steps, the frame-manager no-match clear.
5. **Land the contract.** The normative `GUIDE.txt` entry, `Step Run` and `Step List` into `CONTEXT.md`, and the two RFC-01 amendments written into RFC-01.

Phase 1 is the one that can go wrong quietly, so it deserves its own PR and its own review before anything depends on it.

## Smaller, if you want them

- **`bt --version` should probably be in the skill's own verb block**, not only in prose. Minor.
- **`test_e2e_camoufox.py` tests a deleted surface.** It exercises `CamoufoxSession.call_tool` with MCP-era tool names. It passes and costs a second, but it is an oracle for a parity baseline, not the product. Now that a real launch is covered, decide whether it still earns its place.

## What I would do

Phase 1, as its own PR, with a cross-family review before it merges. Say the word and I will start; the phasing above is my recommendation, not a decision I have made for you.

``passthrough.send``, ``events.wait``, ``list_verbs.console_list``/

four modules (RFC-01 #37/#42/#43/#50), differing only in the one line that
uses the attached session. This module is the single owner of that protocol:

  that opens the connection, resolves the target, attaches, yields
  ``(cdp, session_id)`` to the caller's body, and always detaches afterward,
  best-effort.
- :func:`cli_cdp_errors` is the matching error-mapping seam: a decorator for
  each verb's public sync function that maps the seam's own failures --
  target resolution, no-page, CDP, connection, and unknown-instance errors --
  to ``LifecycleError`` (CLI exit 1). Verb-specific errors (``UsageError``,
  ``WaitTimeout``) are not touched by this decorator and pass through exactly
  as each verb already raises them.

-----------------------
Before this seam existed, ``passthrough._send_one_shot`` and
``curated._capture_screenshot`` raised ``LifecycleError("No page targets in
browser")`` directly, while ``events._wait_one_shot`` and
``list_verbs._collect_one_shot`` raised ``core.errors.NoPageError()`` (caught
one level up and mapped to ``LifecycleError``). Both already reach the same
outcome -- CLI exit 1 with a "no pages" diagnostic -- so there is no behavior
to preserve by keeping two spellings. The seam raises the vendored
``NoPageError`` (it is the specific, already-existing domain error for this
condition) and lets :func:`cli_cdp_errors` do the ``LifecycleError`` mapping,
matching how it already maps ``AmbiguousTargetError``/``TargetNotFoundError``.

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import functools
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

    from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Callable

from .core.attach import AmbiguousTargetError, TargetNotFoundError, resolve_target
from .core.cdp_client import CDPClient, get_ws_url_async
from .core.errors import CDPError, NoPageError
from .core.registry import InstanceNotFoundError
from .lifecycle import LifecycleError


@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def one_shot_page_session(
    port: int,
    target_spec: str | None,
    target_by: str | None,
    *,
    external: bool = False,
) -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[CDPClient, str]]:
    """Connect, resolve a page target, attach, yield the session, detach.

    Opens the browser-level ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient`` connection, lists
    targets, sorts the page targets deterministically by target ID, resolves
    one against ``target_spec``/``target_by`` (``core.attach.resolve_target``
    -- ``AmbiguousTargetError``/``TargetNotFoundError`` propagate unchanged),
    attaches an isolated flattened ``Target`` session, and yields
    ``(cdp, session_id)`` to the body. The session is always detached in a
    ``finally``, best-effort, whether the body returns or raises.

    the module docstring for why this is the one no-page spelling now).

    registry. A failed connection then also reports who holds the port and what
    profile directory they hold, because there is no registry entry to compare
    against and no ``bt status`` row to look the browser up in (#97).
    """
    try:
        browser_ws_url = await get_ws_url_async(port=port, target_type="browser")
    except ConnectionError as exc:
        raise ConnectionError(
            connection_failure_message(port=port, cause=exc.__cause__, external=external)
        ) from exc
    async with CDPClient(ws_url=browser_ws_url) as cdp:
        targets_result = await cdp.send(method="Target.getTargets")
        target_infos: list[dict[str, Any]] = targets_result.get("targetInfos", [])

        def _target_id(t: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
            return t.get("targetId", "")

        page_targets = sorted(
            (t for t in target_infos if t.get("type") == "page"),
            key=_target_id,
        )
        if not page_targets:
            raise NoPageError()

        target_id = resolve_target(
            page_targets=page_targets,
            target_spec=target_spec,
            target_by=target_by,
        )

        session_result = await cdp.send(
            method="Target.attachToTarget",
            params={"targetId": target_id, "flatten": True},
        )
        session_id = session_result["sessionId"]
        try:
            yield cdp, session_id
        finally:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await cdp.send(
                    method="Target.detachFromTarget",
                    params={"sessionId": session_id},
                )

    async def send(
        self,
        method: str,
        params: dict | None = None,
        session_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Send a CDP command and await the response.

        Raises CDPError for protocol errors.
        Raises ConnectionError if not connected or connection lost.
        """
        if not self._connected:
            raise ConnectionError("Not connected to CDP WebSocket")

        self._next_id += 1
        msg_id = self._next_id
        message: dict = {"id": msg_id, "method": method}
        if params is not None:
            message["params"] = params
        if session_id is not None:
            message["sessionId"] = session_id

        future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()
        self._pending[msg_id] = future

        try:
            await self._ws.send(json.dumps(message))
        except Exception as exc:
            self._pending.pop(msg_id, None)
            self._connected = False

"""The handler's client, backed by an attached Target session.

RFC-03 requires a Step Run to hold one browser-level CDP connection with one
flattened ``Target`` session, and requires the run's **CDPRuntime, and
therefore its frame manager, to be built over that attached session** rather
than over a page-level WebSocket. That is a change to how ``CDPHandler``
connects, and the RFC states it as a contract requirement without phasing.
This module is the first phase of meeting it.

Why an adapter rather than a rewrite
------------------------------------
Two clients exist and they are not interchangeable:

- ``cdp_client.CDPClient`` opens a **page-level** socket, sends with no
  ``sessionId``, and registers event handlers with no session filter. The
  handler and everything under it use this one.
- ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient`` opens a **browser-level** socket and carries a
  ``sessionId`` on every send and every event. ``one_shot_page_session`` uses
  this one.

The difference is not cosmetic. ``core/cdp_client.py`` dispatches an event to
a callback only when the callback's filter session is ``None`` or equal to the
event's ``sessionId``, so a page-level connection and a session-filtered
subscriber never meet.

Converging them by threading a ``session_id`` through the handler would touch
about forty call sites across ``cdp_handler``, ``frame_manager``,
``screencast``, ``curated`` and ``interstitial``, in one change, with no
intermediate state that runs. This class instead presents the page-level
client's surface over the browser-level one, so the call sites do not move and
the transport underneath them does. What each caller sends is unchanged; where
it is sent changes.

What this preserves deliberately
--------------------------------
- **The command timeout.** ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient.send`` awaits its
  future with no deadline, so a command Chrome never answers hangs forever.
  The page-level client bounds every command at 30 seconds. Adopting the core
  client without this wrapper would silently drop that bound, so ``send``
  re-applies it here.
- **The exception type.** ``cdp_handler`` and ``screencast`` both catch
  ``cdp_client.CDPError``. The core client raises ``core.errors.CDPError``,
  an unrelated class, and a ``ConnectionError`` when the socket is gone. Both
  are translated, so every existing ``except CDPError`` still fires.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

from .cdp_client import CDPError
from .core.errors import CDPError as CoreCDPError

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .core.cdp_client import CDPClient as CoreCDPClient

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Matches ``cdp_client.CDPClient``'s default. A command that never returns is
#: a hung invocation, and the page-level client has always bounded it.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0


class AttachedSessionClient:
    """``cdp_client.CDPClient``'s surface over one attached Target session.

    Wraps a connected ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient`` and the ``sessionId`` of a
    flattened ``Target`` session on it. Every send carries that session, and
    every event subscription filters on it.

    The lifetime of the connection and the session belongs to whoever opened
    them, which is ``one_shot_page_session``. This object never closes either.
    """

    def __init__(self, client: CoreCDPClient, session_id: str) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._session_id = session_id
        self._closed = False

    @property
    def session_id(self) -> str:
        """The attached session every send and subscription carries."""
        return self._session_id

    @property
    def connected(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the underlying connection is usable.

        ``CDPHandler.available`` reads this, and ``curated`` polls that to
        decide the handler came up, so it has to mean the same thing it did
        on the page-level client.
        """
        return not self._closed and bool(getattr(self._client, "_connected", False))

    async def send(
        self,
        method: str,
        params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        timeout: float | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Send one command over the attached session and return its result.

        Signature and return shape match ``cdp_client.CDPClient.send``, so the
        call sites do not change. ``CDPError`` is raised for a protocol error,
        a lost connection, and a timeout, because that is the one exception
        those call sites catch.
        """
        if self._closed:
            raise CDPError("Not connected to Chrome CDP")
        deadline = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS if timeout is None else timeout
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(
                self._client.send(
                    method=method, params=params, session_id=self._session_id
                ),
                timeout=deadline,
            )
        except CoreCDPError as exc:
            raise CDPError(f"CDP error in {method}: {exc.message}") from exc
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            # The core client keeps the pending future; the session is torn
            # down at the end of the invocation, which collects it.
            raise CDPError(f"CDP command timed out after {deadline}s: {method}") from exc
        except ConnectionError as exc:
            raise CDPError(f"Failed to send CDP command: {exc}") from exc

    def on(self, event: str, handler: Any) -> None:
        """Subscribe to an event on this session only.

        The session filter is the whole point: without it a subscriber on a
        browser-level connection would also see the same event from every
        other attached target.
        """
        self._client.on(event, handler, session_id=self._session_id)

    def off(self, event: str, handler: Any) -> None:
        """Unsubscribe. A handler that was never registered is ignored."""
        self._client.off(event, handler)

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """Mark this client unusable without touching the connection.

        The connection and the session are owned by the context manager that
        opened them. Closing them here would detach a session that manager is
        about to detach again, and close a socket it still holds.
        """
        self._closed = True


__all__ = ["DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "AttachedSessionClient"]

"""The handler's client, backed by an attached Target session.

RFC-03 requires a Step Run to hold one browser-level CDP connection with one
flattened ``Target`` session, and requires the run's **CDPRuntime, and
therefore its frame manager, to be built over that attached session** rather
than over a page-level WebSocket. That is a change to how ``CDPHandler``
connects, and the RFC states it as a contract requirement without phasing.
This module is the first phase of meeting it.

Why an adapter rather than a rewrite
------------------------------------
Two clients exist and they are not interchangeable:

- ``cdp_client.CDPClient`` opens a **page-level** socket, sends with no
  ``sessionId``, and registers event handlers with no session filter. The
  handler and everything under it use this one.
- ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient`` opens a **browser-level** socket and carries a
  ``sessionId`` on every send and every event. ``one_shot_page_session`` uses
  this one.

The difference is not cosmetic. ``core/cdp_client.py`` dispatches an event to
a callback only when the callback's filter session is ``None`` or equal to the
event's ``sessionId``, so a page-level connection and a session-filtered
subscriber never meet.

Converging them by threading a ``session_id`` through the handler would touch
about forty call sites across ``cdp_handler``, ``frame_manager``,
``screencast``, ``curated`` and ``interstitial``, in one change, with no
intermediate state that runs. This class instead presents the page-level
client's surface over the browser-level one, so the call sites do not move and
the transport underneath them does. What each caller sends is unchanged; where
it is sent changes.

What this preserves deliberately
--------------------------------
- **The command timeout.** ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient.send`` awaits its
  future with no deadline, so a command Chrome never answers hangs forever.
  The page-level client bounds every command at 30 seconds. Adopting the core
  client without this wrapper would silently drop that bound, so ``send``
  re-applies it here.
- **The exception type.** ``cdp_handler`` and ``screencast`` both catch
  ``cdp_client.CDPError``. The core client raises ``core.errors.CDPError``,
  an unrelated class, and a ``ConnectionError`` when the socket is gone. Both
  are translated, so every existing ``except CDPError`` still fires.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

from .cdp_client import CDPError
from .core.errors import CDPError as CoreCDPError

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .core.cdp_client import CDPClient as CoreCDPClient

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Matches ``cdp_client.CDPClient``'s default. A command that never returns is
#: a hung invocation, and the page-level client has always bounded it.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0


class AttachedSessionClient:
    """``cdp_client.CDPClient``'s surface over one attached Target session.

    Wraps a connected ``core.cdp_client.CDPClient`` and the ``sessionId`` of a
    flattened ``Target`` session on it. Every send carries that session, and
    every event subscription filters on it.

    The lifetime of the connection and the session belongs to whoever opened
    them, which is ``one_shot_page_session``. This object never closes either.
    """

    def __init__(self, client: CoreCDPClient, session_id: str) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._session_id = session_id
        self._closed = False

    @property
    def session_id(self) -> str:
        """The attached session every send and subscription carries."""
        return self._session_id

    @property
    def connected(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the underlying connection is usable.

        ``CDPHandler.available`` reads this, and ``curated`` polls that to
        decide the handler came up, so it has to mean the same thing it did
        on the page-level client.
        """
        return not self._closed and bool(getattr(self._client, "_connected", False))

    async def send(
        self,
        method: str,
        params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        timeout: float | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Send one command over the attached session and return its result.

        Signature and return shape match ``cdp_client.CDPClient.send``, so the
        call sites do not change. ``CDPError`` is raised for a protocol error,
        a lost connection, and a timeout, because that is the one exception
        those call sites catch.
        """
        if self._closed:
            raise CDPError("Not connected to Chrome CDP")
        deadline = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS if timeout is None else timeout
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(
                self._client.send(
                    method=method, params=params, session_id=self._session_id
                ),
                timeout=deadline,
            )
        except CoreCDPError as exc:
            raise CDPError(f"CDP error in {method}: {exc.message}") from exc
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            # The core client keeps the pending future; the session is torn
            # down at the end of the invocation, which collects it.
            raise CDPError(f"CDP command timed out after {deadline}s: {method}") from exc
        except ConnectionError as exc:
            raise CDPError(f"Failed to send CDP command: {exc}") from exc

    def on(self, event: str, handler: Any) -> None:
        """Subscribe to an event on this session only.

        The session filter is the whole point: without it a subscriber on a
        browser-level connection would also see the same event from every
        other attached target.
        """
        self._client.on(event, handler, session_id=self._session_id)

    def off(self, event: str, handler: Any) -> None:
        """Unsubscribe. A handler that was never registered is ignored."""
        self._client.off(event, handler)

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """Mark this client unusable without touching the connection.

        The connection and the session are owned by the context manager that
        opened them. Closing them here would detach a session that manager is
        about to detach again, and close a socket it still holds.
        """
        self._closed = True


__all__ = ["DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "AttachedSessionClient"]

#!/bin/zsh # Exercise every handler-routed verb against a live browser and print a # normalised transcript. Run on main and on the branch; the transcripts must # match except for values that are inherently per-run (uids, ids, timings). set -u BT="$1" # path to the bt to exercise OUT="$2" # transcript path PAGE="file:///tmp/nine/parent.html" mkdir -p /tmp/nine cat > /tmp/nine/child.html <<'EOF' child

child frame

EOF cat > /tmp/nine/parent.html <<'EOF' parent EOF launch=$("$BT" launch --headless 2>&1) I=$(printf '%s' "$launch" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["name"])') norm() { # Strip what legitimately varies run to run so the diff shows behaviour. python3 -c ' import re, sys t = sys.stdin.read() t = re.sub(r"[0-9A-F]{12,}-", "-", t) # uid doc tokens t = re.sub(r"\"targetId\": \"[0-9A-F]+\"", "\"targetId\": \"\"", t) t = re.sub(r"[0-9A-F]{32}", "", t) t = re.sub(r"\d+\.\d+", "", t) # timings, coords t = re.sub(r"\b\d{3,}\b", "", t) # ports, pids, sizes t = re.sub(r"/tmp/[a-z0-9-]+/session-\w+", "", t) t = re.sub(r"camoufox-\w+", "camoufox-", t) print(t.strip()) ' } { echo "### navigate" "$BT" "$I" Page.navigate "{\"url\": \"$PAGE\"}" 2>&1 | norm sleep 1 echo "### snapshot" "$BT" "$I" snapshot 2>&1 | norm echo "### wait-idle" "$BT" "$I" wait-idle 2>&1 | norm echo "### wait-stable" "$BT" "$I" wait-stable 2>&1 | norm echo "### frames list" "$BT" "$I" frames list 2>&1 | norm echo "### frames select child" "$BT" "$I" frames select child 2>&1 | norm echo "### frames reset" "$BT" "$I" frames reset 2>&1 | norm echo "### storage get --key child" "$BT" "$I" storage get --key child 2>&1 | norm echo "### storage get (no key, expect exit 1)" "$BT" "$I" storage get >/dev/null 2>/tmp/nine/sg.err; echo "exit=$?" norm < /tmp/nine/sg.err echo "### detect --no-wait" "$BT" "$I" detect --no-wait 2>&1 | norm echo "### click (uid from a fresh snapshot)" UID_B=$("$BT" "$I" snapshot 2>/dev/null | python3 -c ' import json,re,sys s=json.load(sys.stdin)["snapshot"] m=re.search(r"\[uid=([0-9A-F]+-\d+)\] button", s) print(m.group(1) if m else "")') if [ -n "$UID_B" ]; then "$BT" "$I" click --uid "$UID_B" 2>&1 | norm; else echo "NO BUTTON UID"; fi echo "### fill" UID_T=$("$BT" "$I" snapshot 2>/dev/null | python3 -c ' import json,re,sys s=json.load(sys.stdin)["snapshot"] m=re.search(r"\[uid=([0-9A-F]+-\d+)\] textbox", s) print(m.group(1) if m else "")') if [ -n "$UID_T" ]; then "$BT" "$I" fill --uid "$UID_T" --text hello 2>&1 | norm; else echo "NO TEXTBOX UID"; fi echo "### fill landed?" "$BT" "$I" Runtime.evaluate '{"expression":"document.getElementById(\"t\").value","returnByValue":true}' 2>&1 | norm echo "### two fills from ONE snapshot (the v6 UID rule)" SNAP=$("$BT" "$I" snapshot 2>/dev/null) U1=$(printf '%s' "$SNAP" | python3 -c ' import json,re,sys s=json.load(sys.stdin)["snapshot"] m=re.search(r"\[uid=([0-9A-F]+-\d+)\] textbox", s) print(m.group(1) if m else "")') "$BT" "$I" fill --uid "$U1" --text one >/dev/null 2>&1 "$BT" "$I" fill --uid "$U1" --text two 2>&1 | norm "$BT" "$I" Runtime.evaluate '{"expression":"document.getElementById(\"t\").value","returnByValue":true}' 2>&1 | norm echo "### stale uid after navigation (expect exit 1)" "$BT" "$I" Page.navigate '{"url":"about:blank"}' >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 0.6 "$BT" "$I" click --uid "$UID_B" >/dev/null 2>/tmp/nine/stale.err; echo "exit=$?" norm < /tmp/nine/stale.err echo "### screencast" "$BT" "$I" Page.navigate "{\"url\": \"$PAGE\"}" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 0.8 rm -rf /tmp/nine/cast; "$BT" "$I" screencast --dir /tmp/nine/cast --duration 2 2>&1 | norm echo "frames written: $(ls /tmp/nine/cast/*.jpg 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ' | sed 's/[0-9]\+/SOME/')" echo "manifest: $([ -f /tmp/nine/cast/frames.json ] && echo yes || echo no)" echo "### screenshot (One-Shot Session verb, must be unaffected)" "$BT" "$I" screenshot --path /tmp/nine/s.png 2>&1 | norm echo "png: $([ -s /tmp/nine/s.png ] && echo yes || echo no)" echo "### target resolution: --target 1" "$BT" "$I" snapshot --target 1 2>&1 | head -c 200 | norm echo "### target resolution: bad target (expect failure)" "$BT" "$I" snapshot --target 99 >/dev/null 2>/tmp/nine/bt.err; echo "exit=$?" norm < /tmp/nine/bt.err } > "$OUT" 2>&1 "$BT" stop "$I" >/dev/null 2>&1 echo "transcript: $OUT"

import pathlib
f = pathlib.Path("src/browser_tools/cdp_handler.py"); s = f.read_text()
old = """            cdp, session_id = await self._sessions.enter_async_context(
                one_shot_page_session(port, self._target_spec, None)
            )"""
new = """            # `target_by` is not optional when a spec is given: the seam
            # dispatches on it and rejects None. The page-level path derived
            # it the same way (`cdp_client._resolve_among`), so --target 3
            # and --target B343DD76 keep meaning what they meant.
            target_by = None
            if self._target_spec is not None:
                target_by = "index" if self._target_spec.isdigit() else "id"

            cdp, session_id = await self._sessions.enter_async_context(
                one_shot_page_session(port, self._target_spec, target_by)
            )"""
assert old in s
f.write_text(s.replace(old, new, 1))
print("target_by fixed")
PY
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check src/ 2>&1|tail -1

#!/bin/zsh
# Per-invocation cost of a handler-routed verb, before and after the
# transport change. The attached-session path does one extra round trip
# (Target.attachToTarget) and one fewer HTTP page lookup, so this measures
# whether that trade costs anything a caller would notice.
set -u
BT="$1"; N="${2:-12}"; OUT="$3"
zmodload zsh/datetime

launch=$("$BT" launch --headless 2>&1)
I=$(printf '%s' "$launch" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["name"])')
"$BT" "$I" Page.navigate '{"url":"file:///tmp/nine/parent.html"}' >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 1

# Warm once so neither side pays first-call import costs in the sample.
"$BT" "$I" snapshot >/dev/null 2>&1

: > "$OUT"
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
  t0=$EPOCHREALTIME
  "$BT" "$I" snapshot >/dev/null 2>&1
  t1=$EPOCHREALTIME
  printf 'snapshot\t%d\t%.1f\n' "$i" $(( (t1 - t0) * 1000 )) >> "$OUT"
done
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
  t0=$EPOCHREALTIME
  "$BT" "$I" frames list >/dev/null 2>&1
  t1=$EPOCHREALTIME
  printf 'frames-list\t%d\t%.1f\n' "$i" $(( (t1 - t0) * 1000 )) >> "$OUT"
done

"$BT" stop "$I" >/dev/null 2>&1
python3 - "$OUT" <<'PY'
import statistics, sys, collections
rows = collections.defaultdict(list)
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    verb, _, ms = line.split("\t")
    rows[verb].append(float(ms))
for verb, xs in rows.items():
    print(f"{verb:12} n={len(xs):2}  median={statistics.median(xs):7.1f} ms  min={min(xs):7.1f}  max={max(xs):7.1f}")
PY

"""`AttachedSessionClient` presents the page-level surface over a session.

The adapter exists so the handler's forty-odd call sites keep their shape
while the transport under them changes (RFC-03, "One CDPRuntime for the
run"). These tests pin the three things that silently break if it is wrong:
the session reaches the wire, the exception type stays the one callers
catch, and the command timeout the page-level client always had survives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

import pytest

from browser_tools.attached_session import (
    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    AttachedSessionClient,
)
from browser_tools.cdp_client import CDPError
from browser_tools.core.errors import CDPError as CoreCDPError


class FakeCore:
    """Records what a core client would have been asked to do."""

    def __init__(self, *, result=None, raises=None, hang=False):
        self.sent: list[dict] = []
        self.subscriptions: list[tuple[str, object, str | None]] = []
        self.removed: list[tuple[str, object]] = []
        self.closed = False
        self._connected = True
        self._result = result if result is not None else {"ok": True}
        self._raises = raises
        self._hang = hang

    async def send(self, method, params=None, session_id=None):
        self.sent.append(
            {"method": method, "params": params, "session_id": session_id}
        )
        if self._hang:
            await asyncio.Event().wait()
        if self._raises is not None:
            raise self._raises
        return self._result

    def on(self, event, callback, session_id=None):
        self.subscriptions.append((event, callback, session_id))

    def off(self, event, callback):
        self.removed.append((event, callback))

    async def close(self):
        self.closed = True

def core() -> FakeCore:
    return FakeCore()


@pytest.fixture
def client(core: FakeCore) -> AttachedSessionClient:
    return AttachedSessionClient(core, "SESSION-1")


class TestEverySendCarriesTheSession:
    """A send without the session goes to the browser, not the page."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_the_session_id_is_attached(self, client, core):
        await client.send("Page.enable")
        assert core.sent == [
            {"method": "Page.enable", "params": None, "session_id": "SESSION-1"}
        ]

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_params_pass_through_unchanged(self, client, core):
        await client.send("Page.navigate", {"url": "https://example.com"})
        assert core.sent[0]["params"] == {"url": "https://example.com"}

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_the_result_is_returned_as_is(self, core):
        client = AttachedSessionClient(FakeCore(result={"frameTree": {}}), "S")
        assert await client.send("Page.getFrameTree") == {"frameTree": {}}

    def test_the_session_id_is_readable(self, client):
        assert client.session_id == "SESSION-1"


class TestTheExceptionTypeCallersCatch:
    """`cdp_handler` and `screencast` both catch `cdp_client.CDPError`.

    The core client raises an unrelated `core.errors.CDPError` and a bare
    `ConnectionError`. Either would escape every existing handler.

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_a_core_protocol_error_becomes_the_callers_error(self):
        core = FakeCore(raises=CoreCDPError(code=-32000, message="No node"))
        client = AttachedSessionClient(core, "S")
        with pytest.raises(CDPError) as caught:
            await client.send("DOM.querySelector")
        assert "No node" in str(caught.value)

    async def test_a_lost_connection_becomes_the_callers_error(self):
        core = FakeCore(raises=ConnectionError("socket gone"))
        client = AttachedSessionClient(core, "S")
        with pytest.raises(CDPError):
            await client.send("Page.enable")

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_sending_after_disconnect_is_refused(self, client):
        await client.disconnect()
        with pytest.raises(CDPError):
            await client.send("Page.enable")

    """The core client awaits its future with no deadline.

    answers into a hang with no diagnostic.

    def test_the_default_matches_the_page_level_client(self):
        from browser_tools.cdp_client import CDPClient

        import inspect

        page_default = inspect.signature(CDPClient.__init__).parameters["timeout"].default
        assert DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS == page_default

    async def test_a_hung_command_raises_rather_than_hanging(self):
        client = AttachedSessionClient(FakeCore(hang=True), "S")
        with pytest.raises(CDPError) as caught:
            await client.send("Page.enable", timeout=0.05)
        assert "timed out" in str(caught.value)

    async def test_the_caller_can_override_the_deadline(self):
        client = AttachedSessionClient(FakeCore(hang=True), "S")
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        started = loop.time()
        with pytest.raises(CDPError):
            await client.send("Page.enable", timeout=0.02)
        assert loop.time() - started < 1.0, "the override was ignored"

    """A browser-level connection sees every attached target's events."""

    def test_on_registers_with_the_session_filter(self, client, core):
        def handler(_params): ...

        assert core.subscriptions == [
            ("Page.frameNavigated", handler, "SESSION-1")
        ]

    def test_off_removes_the_handler(self, client, core):
        def handler(_params): ...

        client.off("Page.frameNavigated", handler)
        assert core.removed == [("Page.frameNavigated", handler)]

    """`one_shot_page_session` opened the connection and detaches it."""

    async def test_disconnect_does_not_close_the_connection(self, client, core):
        await client.disconnect()
        assert core.closed is False, "the adapter closed a socket it does not own"

    def test_connected_tracks_the_underlying_client(self, client, core):
        assert client.connected is True
        core._connected = False
        assert client.connected is False

    async def test_connected_is_false_after_disconnect(self, client):
        await client.disconnect()
        assert client.connected is False

    `ValueError: Unknown target_by: None` when a spec is given without one.
    The page-level path derived it from the spec, so `--target 1` and
    `--target <id>` both worked; passing None broke every `--target`.
    """

        derived = None if spec is None else ("index" if spec.isdigit() else "id")
        assert derived == expected

    def test_the_page_level_path_used_that_rule(self):
        """Pinned against the source it was copied from, not from memory."""
        from pathlib import Path

        import browser_tools

        source = (
            Path(browser_tools.__file__).parent / "cdp_client.py"
        ).read_text()
        assert 'target_by="index" if target_spec.isdigit() else "id"' in source

@~/.agents/GLOBAL.md

# Claude Code Instructions

These instructions apply only to Claude Code, layered on the global
instructions imported above.

## Model selection and delegation

Two skills own this; nothing here restates them.

- `choose-model` picks the route (model through harness) from its
  registry. Same query, same answer. Query it before any delegation where
  the model is not pinned by the user or by the calling skill's own spec.

  Every `Agent` spawn, every `Workflow` `agent()` call, and every agent
  started in a terminal you control is a delegation. The last one includes
  `herdr agent start` and any successor session you launch to carry on work.
  This includes spawns you would describe as fanning out your own reading,
  searching, or exploring. There is no unrouted subagent. A pane is not an
  exemption: `--kind claude` selects a harness, not a model, so a launch with
  no model argument inherits whatever that harness defaults to. A spawn that
  carries no explicit `model:` inherits the session model, which the
  registry ranks last for most task types - so an unrouted fan-out is not
  neutral, it is the worst route chosen by accident.

  The query is its own tool block and precedes the block that spawns.
  Never send the query and the spawn together. Bundling independent calls
  is right in general and wrong here: the spawn depends on the query.
- `delegate` runs the pick: your subagent tool for a same-harness route,
  `scripts/delegate.ts` over `hcn run` for every other route, walking the
  fallbacks on hcn's typed failure classes and reporting which route
  actually produced the result. Never a raw `codex exec`, `pi -p`, or
  `muse exec`.

Cross-family reviewers: query with `excludeFamilies` set to the
implementer's family. Never silently run an adversarial role on the same
family as the majority; if cross-family was unavailable, say so in the
synthesis.

Claude Code mechanics, which the skills cannot carry because they are
harness-neutral:

- **Same-harness routes** (`harness: claude`) run through the `Agent` or
  `Workflow` `model:` parameter with the route's `modelId` and `effort`.
  Pass the model explicitly on every spawn: subagents inherit the session
  model when `model:` is omitted, so omitting it silently routes the work
  to whatever the session happens to be running. Label the spawn with the
  route. Tool scope there comes from the agent
  type, not the call: `delegate.ts --plan` shows the access the task
  defaults to; `read` means a read-only agent type (Explore, or a project
  agent defined with read tools), `write` means general-purpose.
- **Every other route runs through a wrapper.** The `model:` parameter
  takes Claude models only, so a non-Claude route inside a Workflow stage
  or a background Agent is a `model:'sonnet'`, `effort:'low'` wrapper
  whose whole job is: write the brief to a file, run
  `npx tsx ~/.agents/skills/delegate/scripts/delegate.ts --choice <choice.json> --brief <brief.md> --out <report.json>`
  via Bash, and return the report. Use `schema` on the wrapper when
  structured output is needed. **Label the wrapper with the route**,
  e.g. `{label:'glm-5.3@pi:impl'}`, `{label:'gpt-5.6-sol@codex:review-auth'}`:

  the check passed.

  word-split, and an unmatched glob is a hard error rather than a literal.

  arguments carrying globs. A loop feeding `cmd $arg` turns every multi-word

  wrong answer.

  `EnterWorktree` and `git worktree add` start from HEAD and carry none of the

  and commit are forbidden: create the worktree from HEAD; apply

  untracked files, excluding caches; add the worktree directory to the main

  verify stay inside the worktree**: git combined with subshells or process
  substitution, heredoc-written programs, and programs computed at runtime.
  Write the command to a file with the Write tool and run it plainly

These instructions apply across local repositories and tools on this machine.

- When writing commit messages, NEVER auto-add your agent name as co-author.
- Never manually modify CHANGELOG.md files or any files marked as
  auto-generated.
- When making technical decisions, give development cost little weight.

  maintainability.

  standards when applicable. Wait for their answer before choosing the

A possibility is not a mandate. That a capability can be built, that a
reviewer says it is missing, or that a planning session surfaced it does
not mean it belongs in the product. Before any functionality decision (what
the product does for its users is about to be added, removed, or changed),
run the fit check. Reorganization (refactor, cleanup, lint) is outside it.

- Who uses this? Name the actual users and what they do with it.
- What is the product for? One sentence, from `CONTEXT.md`, the README,
  or the request. If none states it, ask before building.
- Does the candidate serve that purpose? No: decline it and record why.
  Unclear: it is the user's decision, with a recommended answer.
- Which way does it move the scope? Widen, hold, or narrow. Name the
  direction; widen and narrow are the user's call. Narrow is a valid
  answer.

The full ruleset, the moments it fires, and the record a declined
candidate leaves are the `fit-check` skill.

## Task Artifacts

A harness scratchpad or temp directory does not survive the session. Files
there can be gone by the next session, including one that resumes the same
work. Keep throwaway output there, and nothing else.

A task's decision ledger, its evidence (scripts, captures, measurements),
any git worktree or working checkout the task created, any branch not yet
merged, and any report a later reader must reach go in a durable place
instead.

git-ignored. It sits beside the code it is about, `git status` keeps it
visible, and cleanup is one directory removal in one place. Use
`~/.agents/tasks/<task>/` only when the work has no single home repository
or spans several. Name that path in the task's checkpoint and in the final
report, so the record is findable after the session ends.

parent's `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. Renaming or moving either side
breaks git commands inside that worktree while leaving its trees and commits
intact. Repair it from the main checkout with

the links and nothing else.

document that points at a git-ignored path resolves on one machine and
nowhere else. Commit that evidence into the repository, or cite the
finding rather than the path.

  each level apply tracked guidance first, then that scope's

  user. Publish under the matching scope, e.g. `@dungle-scrubs/<name>`.
  Never guess a package name or scope - this is it.
- Never distribute my open source projects through Homebrew: no formula,
  no cask, no `brew install` line in their install instructions. Prefer
  npm for anything Node/Bun-adjacent, else a direct install script.
  Installing other people's tools with Homebrew stays fine.

Under `~/dev`; useful context for agent sessions.

- `~/dev/launchdawg` - reconciler for macOS user LaunchAgents
  (`~/.config/launchdawg/services.yml`).
- `~/dev/opchain` - CLI for 1Password service-account workflows.
- `~/dev/ansible` - source of truth for the macOS Kanata unit. Before
  Kanata setup or recovery, install its skill with the repository's
  `kanata_skill` Ansible tag and start a new agent session.
- `~/dev/skills` - source of truth for the shared skill library, deployed
  to `~/.agents/skills` by its link script. `~/dev/skills-old` is
  abandoned; do not work in it, and nothing deploys from it.

Load on the trigger, not otherwise.

| When a task involves | Read |
|---|---|
| Host selection, remote access, machine capabilities, keeping dev machines synchronized | `~/.agents/references/home-network.md` |
| Running a model on a local endpoint, or picking the local model or machine for some work | `~/.agents/references/local-inference.md` |
| Agent hooks, agent config files, or a tool that wants to install itself into an agent | `~/.agents/references/agents-setup.md` |

## Local Ports

Before starting, configuring, or changing a local development server, read
`~/.agents/PORTS.md`. Use the assigned port when the service is listed;
give a new long-running service an unused port from the reserved range and
add its row so the registry stays the source of truth. Bind every local
server to loopback (`127.0.0.1`), never to all interfaces; a wider bind
needs the user's explicit request, scoped to that one server.

## Private Data and Local Inference

The privacy override: work that would put secret material into a hosted
model's context runs on a local model instead. Secret material: environment
variables and `.env` files, API tokens, credentials, private keys,
`1Password` output, terminal output from a production host, and anything
the user calls private. Hosted models are disqualified, including
whichever agent is reading this. Privacy work never reroutes to a hosted
model, even when no local model is reachable: say the work cannot be done
on this machine instead.

Credential and key fields inside local tool stores are secret material too,
for example a Cursor chat store's `blobEncryptionKey`. Explore such a store
by printing structure only: field names, shapes, lengths, counts. Never
select or decode the credential value in a hosted session; tool output
enters the model's context when it prints. If the value itself must be
read, run that read on a local model with a pointer to the file.

the input until the gate stops matching. Renaming a credential file, moving
it, or splitting the command so the pattern no longer fires leaves the same
value flowing into the same hosted context, with the record now showing a
pass. If the denial looks wrong, say so and leave it in place; a gate whose
false positives get worked around is a gate that protects nothing.

`choose-model` query carrying `privacy: secret`: the only eligible routes
are local, and the walk adds the containment flags itself. Compose the
prompt with pointers, not payloads - file paths, command names, line
numbers - and let the local model read the secret material on-machine. A
prompt that quotes the token has already leaked it, whichever model
answers.

air port forward, and the Herdr pane recipe are in
`~/.agents/references/local-inference.md` under "Private data".

These are Codex-only mechanics. They live here because `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`
is a symlink to this file and Codex has no import directive.

single operation, so a rewrite is one `*** Update File` hunk, never
`*** Delete File` followed by `*** Add File`. Every `@@` needs at least one

next `*** Update File:` header and fails the whole call. The call is atomic,
so one stale hunk in the fourth file discards the first three, and the error
names only the file that failed, which is usually not the one at the top of
the patch. Send one file per envelope.

`exec_command` owns every process it starts, and kills it when that call
returns. A daemon started inside one call is gone by the next: the launcher
reports a PID and exits 0, then the process is not running and nothing can
attach to it. Keep a long-lived process alive one of two ways: hold the exec
session open and drive it with `write_stdin` against its `session_id`, or
start it in a Herdr pane. Relaunching is not the fix; the second launch dies
the same way.

`rm -rf` anywhere rejects the whole `exec_command` call, including every
unrelated command bundled with it. Delete with `/usr/bin/trash`, and never
bundle a delete with work you cannot afford to lose.

## Tool Proxy

If the tool-proxy MCP is available, call `discover_tools` with a
plain-language description of the task before using any CLI or raw API for
an external service. Do not guess tool names; discovery expands from there.
Common triggers: Vercel, web scraping, pen.dev,
Algolia, GA4, GCS, Google Search Console, GTM, Intercom,
Laravel Cloud, Namecheap, Notion, Rack Warehouse, Postgres, Reviewsion,
Sentry, Shopify, Vultr, WorkOS.

## Browser Automation

Two CLIs cover this. They are not interchangeable. Pick by task.

`chrome-devtools-axi` is the default. It drives a page: `open`, `snapshot`,
`click`, `fill`, `screenshot`, and a multi-step flow through `run`. It is the
only one with performance tooling: `lighthouse`, `perf-start` / `perf-stop` /
`perf-insight`, `heap`, and `emulate` for viewport, network, CPU and
geolocation. `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_AUTO_CONNECT=1` attaches to the running
Chrome, so a logged-in session needs no profile copy.

`browser-tools` (`bt`, skill at `~/.agents/skills/browser-tools`) takes the
task when it needs any of these:

- a raw CDP method no verb covers, or the live protocol schema (`bt help`),
- an event stream, or a blocking wait on one event (`attach`, `wait`),
- a named persistent profile, or several browsers at once,
- an anti-detect engine (Camoufox) or a fingerprint profile,
- `screencast`, `frames`, `storage get`, or interstitial `detect`,
- any run made while the user is at the keyboard. `browser-tools` refuses

  window in the background. `chrome-devtools-axi` guarantees neither.

`browser-tools` is CLI only. Its MCP front was deleted in RFC-01 Phase 5.

The `chrome-devtools-axi` startup banner says to prefer it over other browser
automation tools. That sentence is the tool's own description of itself. This
section supersedes it.

## GitHub

Handle GitHub with the `gh` CLI, which is signed in as `dungle-scrubs`.
Prefer the `gh-axi` wrapper where it covers the command; it loads at
session start and prints the repository, open issues, and open PRs. Add
`--json` for output an agent parses. `gh api` reaches anything the
subcommands miss.

## Communication

Never manage, validate, or comment on the user's emotions. You are not a
person, and the user does not want your read on how they feel.

When the user asks a question while a task runs, answer it in the next
message, then continue the task. Never hold the answer for the end-of-turn
summary. If the answer depends on work not yet done, say so and say when
the answer will come.

Report a privacy incident in the message where it happens. A credential
printed into a hosted session, a secret file read in full, or private data
sent outward is named immediately with what to rotate, then the task
continues. Never hold it for the end-of-turn summary.

State a cause only when the evidence establishes it. An explanation
already in hand is not evidence for the case in front of you: check the
current one before reaching for it. Say which stage is confirmed and which
is not. Absent records establish nothing - an empty log is not proof that a
thing failed, nor that it succeeded. Never call partial evidence
confirmation; "the logs confirm it" over a zero-byte file is a claim about
the file, not about the event.

When you write a file for the user to read - a report, a plan, a draft, a
set of findings - open it with `open "<absolute path>"` before you present
it, and keep the path in the reply. The system opener picks the user's own
app for that file type, so name no editor. A file meant for browser viewing
goes through the `open-in-browser` skill instead. A file written for an
agent or a tool to consume stays closed. When the opener fails, say the file
did not open.

When a command needs to run, run it yourself. Hand a command to the user
only when the agent genuinely cannot run it: interactive authentication
(`gcloud auth login`), commands that must outlive the session with no
service manager available, or actions the user must perform under their
own identity. "It is the user's dev server" is not a reason - kill the
stale process and start the right one.

A command that cannot run in the agent's own shell but does not need
`sudo` still runs without the user when Herdr is available (the `herdr`
skill is installed and `HERDR_ENV=1`). Create a new Herdr pane, run the
command there, read the pane to confirm the command succeeded, then close
the pane. This rule is the user's explicit request to use Herdr for that
case. The agent reads the pane output, so the command must not print
secret material; redirect it to a file instead. A command that a hook or
permission gate denied does not go to a pane: the denial is deliberate,
and a pane run goes around it. Hand the command to the user only when it
needs `sudo`, when a gate denied it, when Herdr is not available, or when
the pane run fails.

Ticket succession is authorized the same way. A session working a map,
having recorded its resolution, may start its successor in a Herdr pane and
close its own pane, without asking each time. This rule is the user's
explicit request for that case. It covers only the successor's pane and the
finishing session's own pane; every other pane lifecycle action still needs
its own approval. The finishing session closes itself only when the handoff
is complete and its final message carries nothing recorded nowhere else.

When handing over a command (only in those cases): print the complete
command, copy it to the clipboard with `pbcopy`, and frame it in an ASCII
`+`/`-`/`|` border with `COPIED TO CLIPBOARD` inside the top edge, one
blank bordered line above the command, sized so the command fits on one
line untruncated.

When the user's attention needs to move to a different surface - a served
page, an app window, a canvas, a file - say so before continuing. Open it
when you can. When you cannot bring it into view, print an ASCII box:

```
+--------------------------------------------+
| LOOK HERE - PEN.APP                        |
|                                            |
|  Canvas frame "N2 Gapped Index"            |
|  Bring Pen to the front                    |
+--------------------------------------------+
```

Name the surface, the address or location, and what to do there. Keep an
address stable once given; do not move a served page to a new port. Work
split across two surfaces without naming which one is live leaves the user
guessing, and a moving address makes "look at the page" unusable even when
you do say it.

Voice rules, always on. The named phrasings behind each rule are patterns
in `~/.agents/skills/talk-normal/references/BANNED.md`, enforced by the
phrase gate; the full register is the talk-normal skill.

- Never acknowledge, name, or validate an emotional state, and never
  apologize for the user's feelings. Acknowledge a factual mistake
  plainly and move on.
- No reassurance, empathy statements, or tone-policing; respond to the
  substance only.
- Never call output "honest" or contrast it as "the real X instead of Y";
  state the facts and give the numbers.
- Never announce or grade your own sentence: no "let me be clear," and no
  "worth <verb>ing" in any form, including "worth noting," "worth knowing,"
  "worth flagging," "worth building". Write the sentence.
- Never ascribe wants, feelings, or excitement to yourself; state what
  the change does or what you will do next.
- Never praise, approve of, or grade the user; act on the correction and
  move on.
- Never say "hand-waving" / "hand-wavy"; say plainly what is unspecified,
  unverified, or skipped.
- Plain voice: STE register (short sentences, one idea per sentence,
  plain verbs, present tense where possible), one name per thing from the
  project's `CONTEXT.md` or its canonical term, no analogies or metaphor.
  Plain does not mean thin: keep every decision, reason, and step; put
  overflow detail behind a pointer, never delete it.
