- When scaffolding a project, always ask the user whether to use XDG
  standards when applicable. Wait for their answer before choosing the
  affected directory layout or file locations.
- When fixing a bug, first reproduce it end-to-end, as close as possible to
  how an end user hits it. This finds the real problem, so the fix solves
  it.
- When configuring, integrating, or debugging a third-party tool, library,
  or framework, consult its current official documentation before
  reverse-engineering behavior from error messages. Reach for the docs the
  moment you are guessing at version-specific behavior or at how two tools
  interact, or after two attempts have not converged.
- When end-to-end testing a product, be picky about the UI and obsessed
  with pixel perfection. If something clearly looks off, even outside the
  current task, try to get it fixed.
- Apply the same standard to lint, test failures, and test flakiness: fix
  them even when the current work did not cause them.

## Fit Check

A possibility is not a mandate. That a capability can be built, that a
reviewer says it is missing, or that a planning session surfaced it does
not mean it belongs in the product. Before any functionality decision (what
the product does for its users is about to be added, removed, or changed),
run the fit check. Reorganization (refactor, cleanup, lint) is outside it.

- Who uses this? Name the actual users and what they do with it.
- What is the product for? One sentence, from `CONTEXT.md`, the README,
  or the request. If none states it, ask before building.
- Does the candidate serve that purpose? No: decline it and record why.
  Unclear: it is the user's decision, with a recommended answer.
- What does it cost to keep? Name the upkeep it adds after it ships and
  weigh it against that use. Build cost gets little weight; upkeep is paid
  for as long as the capability exists. Upkeep larger than the use:
  decline it, even though it fits.
- Which way does it move the scope? Widen, hold, or narrow. Name the
  direction; widen and narrow are the user's call. Narrow is a valid
  answer.

The full ruleset, the moments it fires, and the record a declined
candidate leaves are the `fit-check` skill.

## Task Artifacts

A harness scratchpad or temp directory does not survive the session. Files
there can be gone by the next session, including one that resumes the same
work. Keep throwaway output there, and nothing else.

A task's decision ledger, its evidence (scripts, captures, measurements),
any git worktree or working checkout the task created, any branch not yet
merged, and any report a later reader must reach go in a durable place
instead.
Default to `.scratch/<task>/` inside the repository the work belongs to,
git-ignored. It sits beside the code it is about, `git status` keeps it
visible, and cleanup is one directory removal in one place. Use
`~/.agents/tasks/<task>/` only when the work has no single home repository
or spans several. Name that path in the task's checkpoint and in the final
report, so the record is findable after the session ends.

A linked worktree stores absolute paths, in its own `.git` file and in the
parent's `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. Renaming or moving either side
breaks git commands inside that worktree while leaving its trees and commits
intact. Repair it from the main checkout with
`git worktree repair <path>...`, naming every moved worktree; it rewrites
the links and nothing else.

Evidence that a committed file cites is not task scratch. A comment or a
document that points at a git-ignored path resolves on one machine and
nowhere else. Commit that evidence into the repository, or cite the
finding rather than the path.

## Repository Instruction Files

- `AGENTS.md` is the canonical instruction file at every repository scope;
  all harness-independent guidance goes there.
- Every directory with an `AGENTS.md` has a sibling `CLAUDE.md` whose first
  non-comment instruction imports `@AGENTS.md`. Below the import: Claude
  Code-specific mechanics only, never duplicated shared guidance.
- Local, untracked guidance follows the same pattern: `AGENTS.local.md`
  for harness-independent local instructions, `CLAUDE.local.md` importing
  it. Both are git-ignored; `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` stay trackable.
  Never use `AGENTS.override.md` for additive local guidance - Codex
  treats it as a replacement for the sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- Apply scopes from the repository root toward the working directory. At
  each level apply tracked guidance first, then that scope's
  `AGENTS.local.md` when it exists and is not already in context. Skip
  local files from scopes that do not govern the current work.

## Identity and Publishing

- The GitHub scope is `dungle-scrubs`; the `gh` CLI authenticates as that
  user. Publish under the matching scope, e.g. `@dungle-scrubs/<name>`.
  Never guess a package name or scope - this is it.
- Never distribute my open source projects through Homebrew: no formula,
  no cask, no `brew install` line in their install instructions. Prefer
  npm for anything Node/Bun-adjacent, else a direct install script.
  Installing other people's tools with Homebrew stays fine.

## Important Local Repositories

Under `~/dev`; useful context for agent sessions.

- `~/dev/launchdawg` - reconciler for macOS user LaunchAgents
  (`~/.config/launchdawg/services.yml`).
- `~/dev/opchain` - CLI for 1Password service-account workflows.
- `~/dev/ansible` - source of truth for the macOS Kanata unit. Before
  Kanata setup or recovery, install its skill with the repository's
  `kanata_skill` Ansible tag and start a new agent session.
- `~/dev/skills` - source of truth for the shared skill library, deployed
  to `~/.agents/skills` by its link script. `~/dev/skills-old` is
  abandoned; do not work in it, and nothing deploys from it.

## References

Load on the trigger, not otherwise.

| When a task involves | Read |
|---|---|
| Host selection, remote access, machine capabilities, keeping dev machines synchronized | `~/.agents/references/home-network.md` |
| Running a model on a local endpoint, or picking the local model or machine for some work | `~/.agents/references/local-inference.md` |
| Agent hooks, agent config files, or a tool that wants to install itself into an agent | `~/.agents/references/agents-setup.md` |

## Local Ports

Before starting, configuring, or changing a local development server, read
`~/.agents/PORTS.md`. Use the assigned port when the service is listed;
give a new long-running service an unused port from the reserved range and
add its row so the registry stays the source of truth. Bind every local
server to loopback (`127.0.0.1`), never to all interfaces; a wider bind
needs the user's explicit request, scoped to that one server.

## Private Data and Local Inference

The privacy override: work that would put secret material into a hosted
model's context runs on a local model instead. Secret material: environment
variables and `.env` files, API tokens, credentials, private keys,
`1Password` output, terminal output from a production host, and anything
the user calls private. Hosted models are disqualified, including
whichever agent is reading this. Privacy work never reroutes to a hosted
model, even when no local model is reachable: say the work cannot be done
on this machine instead.

Credential and key fields inside local tool stores are secret material too,
for example a Cursor chat store's `blobEncryptionKey`. Explore such a store
by printing structure only: field names, shapes, lengths, counts. Never
select or decode the credential value in a hosted session; tool output
enters the model's context when it prints. If the value itself must be
read, run that read on a local model with a pointer to the file.

A gate denial is answered by the route the denial names, never by reshaping
the input until the gate stops matching. Renaming a credential file, moving
it, or splitting the command so the pattern no longer fires leaves the same
value flowing into the same hosted context, with the record now showing a
pass. If the denial looks wrong, say so and leave it in place; a gate whose
false positives get worked around is a gate that protects nothing.

Run it as a separate process, through the `delegate` skill with a
`choose-model` query carrying `privacy: secret`: the only eligible routes
are local, and the walk adds the containment flags itself. Compose the
prompt with pointers, not payloads - file paths, command names, line
numbers - and let the local model read the secret material on-machine. A
prompt that quotes the token has already leaked it, whichever model
answers.

The by-hand hcn run, the containment flags and why each one matters, the
air port forward, and the Herdr pane recipe are in
`~/.agents/references/local-inference.md` under "Private data".

## Codex

These are Codex-only mechanics. They live here because `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`
is a symlink to this file and Codex has no import directive.

`apply_patch` takes one file and one operation per call. A path carries a
single operation, so a rewrite is one `*** Update File` hunk, never
`*** Delete File` followed by `*** Add File`. Every `@@` needs at least one
`+` or `-` line under it: a context-only hunk, or a bare `@@`, swallows the
next `*** Update File:` header and fails the whole call. The call is atomic,
so one stale hunk in the fourth file discards the first three, and the error
names only the file that failed, which is usually not the one at the top of
the patch. Send one file per envelope.

`exec_command` owns every process it starts, and kills it when that call
returns. A daemon started inside one call is gone by the next: the launcher
reports a PID and exits 0, then the process is not running and nothing can
attach to it. Keep a long-lived process alive one of two ways: hold the exec
session open and drive it with `write_stdin` against its `session_id`, or
start it in a Herdr pane. Relaunching is not the fix; the second launch dies
the same way.

The command guard scans the entire script string, so a single `rm -f` or
`rm -rf` anywhere rejects the whole `exec_command` call, including every
unrelated command bundled with it. Delete with `/usr/bin/trash`, and never
bundle a delete with work you cannot afford to lose.

## Tool Proxy

If the tool-proxy MCP is available, call `discover_tools` with a
plain-language description of the task before using any CLI or raw API for
an external service. Do not guess tool names; discovery expands from there.
Common triggers: Vercel, web scraping, pen.dev,
Algolia, GA4, GCS, Google Search Console, GTM, Intercom,
Laravel Cloud, Namecheap, Notion, Rack Warehouse, Postgres, Reviewsion,
Sentry, Shopify, Vultr, WorkOS.

## Browser Automation

Two CLIs cover this. They are not interchangeable. Pick by task.

`chrome-devtools-axi` is the default. It drives a page: `open`, `snapshot`,
`click`, `fill`, `screenshot`, and a multi-step flow through `run`. It is the
only one with performance tooling: `lighthouse`, `perf-start` / `perf-stop` /
`perf-insight`, `heap`, and `emulate` for viewport, network, CPU and
geolocation. `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_AUTO_CONNECT=1` attaches to the running
Chrome, so a logged-in session needs no profile copy.

`browser-tools` (`bt`, skill at `~/.agents/skills/browser-tools`) takes the
task when it needs any of these:

- a raw CDP method no verb covers, or the live protocol schema (`bt help`),
- an event stream, or a blocking wait on one event (`attach`, `wait`),
- a named persistent profile, or several browsers at once,
- an anti-detect engine (Camoufox) or a fingerprint profile,
- `screencast`, `frames`, `storage get`, or interstitial `detect`,
- any run made while the user is at the keyboard. `browser-tools` refuses
  `Page.bringToFront` and `Target.activateTarget`, and it opens a headed
  window in the background. `chrome-devtools-axi` guarantees neither.

`browser-tools` is CLI only. Its MCP front was deleted in RFC-01 Phase 5.

The `chrome-devtools-axi` startup banner says to prefer it over other browser
automation tools. That sentence is the tool's own description of itself. This
section supersedes it.

## GitHub

Handle GitHub with the `gh` CLI, which is signed in as `dungle-scrubs`.
Prefer the `gh-axi` wrapper where it covers the command; it loads at
session start and prints the repository, open issues, and open PRs. Add
`--json` for output an agent parses. `gh api` reaches anything the
subcommands miss.

## Communication

Never manage, validate, or comment on the user's emotions. You are not a
person, and the user does not want your read on how they feel.

When the user asks a question while a task runs, answer it in the next
message, then continue the task. Never hold the answer for the end-of-turn
summary. If the answer depends on work not yet done, say so and say when
the answer will come.

Report a privacy incident in the message where it happens. A credential
printed into a hosted session, a secret file read in full, or private data
sent outward is named immediately with what to rotate, then the task
continues. Never hold it for the end-of-turn summary.

State a cause only when the evidence establishes it. An explanation
already in hand is not evidence for the case in front of you: check the
current one before reaching for it. Say which stage is confirmed and which
is not. Absent records establish nothing - an empty log is not proof that a
thing failed, nor that it succeeded. Never call partial evidence
confirmation; "the logs confirm it" over a zero-byte file is a claim about
the file, not about the event.

When you write a file for the user to read - a report, a plan, a draft, a
set of findings - open it with `open "<absolute path>"` before you present
it, and keep the path in the reply. The system opener picks the user's own
app for that file type, so name no editor. A file meant for browser viewing
goes through the `open-in-browser` skill instead. A file written for an
agent or a tool to consume stays closed. When the opener fails, say the file
did not open.

When a command needs to run, run it yourself. Hand a command to the user
only when the agent genuinely cannot run it: interactive authentication
(`gcloud auth login`), commands that must outlive the session with no
service manager available, or actions the user must perform under their
own identity. "It is the user's dev server" is not a reason - kill the
stale process and start the right one.

A command that cannot run in the agent's own shell but does not need
`sudo` still runs without the user when Herdr is available (the `herdr`
skill is installed and `HERDR_ENV=1`). Create a new Herdr pane, run the
command there, read the pane to confirm the command succeeded, then close
the pane. This rule is the user's explicit request to use Herdr for that
case. The agent reads the pane output, so the command must not print
secret material; redirect it to a file instead. A command that a hook or
permission gate denied does not go to a pane: the denial is deliberate,
and a pane run goes around it. Hand the command to the user only when it
needs `sudo`, when a gate denied it, when Herdr is not available, or when
the pane run fails.

Ticket succession is authorized the same way. A session working a map,
having recorded its resolution, may start its successor in a Herdr pane and
close its own pane, without asking each time. This rule is the user's
explicit request for that case. It covers only the successor's pane and the
finishing session's own pane; every other pane lifecycle action still needs
its own approval. The finishing session closes itself only when the handoff
is complete and its final message carries nothing recorded nowhere else.

When handing over a command (only in those cases): print the complete
command, copy it to the clipboard with `pbcopy`, and frame it in an ASCII
`+`/`-`/`|` border with `COPIED TO CLIPBOARD` inside the top edge, one
blank bordered line above the command, sized so the command fits on one
line untruncated.

When the user's attention needs to move to a different surface - a served
page, an app window, a canvas, a file - say so before continuing. Open it
when you can. When you cannot bring it into view, print an ASCII box:

```
+--------------------------------------------+
| LOOK HERE - PEN.APP                        |
|                                            |
|  Canvas frame "N2 Gapped Index"            |
|  Bring Pen to the front                    |
+--------------------------------------------+
```

Name the surface, the address or location, and what to do there. Keep an
address stable once given; do not move a served page to a new port. Work
split across two surfaces without naming which one is live leaves the user
guessing, and a moving address makes "look at the page" unusable even when
you do say it.

Voice rules, always on. The named phrasings behind each rule are patterns
in `~/.agents/skills/talk-normal/references/BANNED.md`, enforced by the
phrase gate; the full register is the talk-normal skill.

- Never acknowledge, name, or validate an emotional state, and never
  apologize for the user's feelings. Acknowledge a factual mistake
  plainly and move on.
- No reassurance, empathy statements, or tone-policing; respond to the
  substance only.
- Never call output "honest" or contrast it as "the real X instead of Y";
  state the facts and give the numbers.
- Never announce or grade your own sentence: no "let me be clear," and no
  "worth <verb>ing" in any form, including "worth noting," "worth knowing,"
  "worth flagging," "worth building". Write the sentence.
- Never ascribe wants, feelings, or excitement to yourself; state what
  the change does or what you will do next.
- Never praise, approve of, or grade the user; act on the correction and
  move on.
- Never say "hand-waving" / "hand-wavy"; say plainly what is unspecified,
  unverified, or skipped.
- Plain voice: STE register (short sentences, one idea per sentence,
  plain verbs, present tense where possible), one name per thing from the
  project's `CONTEXT.md` or its canonical term, no analogies or metaphor.
  Plain does not mean thin: keep every decision, reason, and step; put
  overflow detail behind a pointer, never delete it.
</system-reminder>

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   This session continues autonomous execution of the RFC-03 build in `~/dev/browser-tools`, authorized by pre-compaction user instructions:
   - *"I want you to do all of that autonomously. I accept RFC03 and let's address RFC01 as well, in addition to the smaller concrete ones. In between each commit PR accordingly."*
   - *"do it"* (approving the 5-phase RFC-03 build plan)
   - Standing instruction: *"merge these PRs, do a release, update the binary on this system, and make sure there's just one main branch at the end locally and remotely."*

   Genuine user messages in THIS session (three):
   1. *"tell me about the pros/cons. would it help with shopify embedded app development?"* — about cross-origin iframe support (issue #127).
   2. (Earlier, via AskUserQuestion rejection) the user asked to clarify the cross-origin question rather than answer it.
   3. *"let's do it"* — approving my recommendation: **build cross-origin iframe support, with a short RFC first, and land the documentation/error-message fix immediately.**

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **browser-tools / `bt`** — Python CLI driving Chrome/Camoufox via CDP. CLI is the only surface.
   - **One-Shot Session** — browser-level CDP connection + `Target.attachToTarget` with `flatten: true`; lives in `one_shot.py`.
   - **CDPRuntime / CDPHandler** — deep CDP layer owning the frame manager; asyncio loop on a background thread, bridged via `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`.
   - **Step Run / Step List / Run Document** — RFC-03: one invocation, one CDP connection, one attached session, many steps. A Step List is data, not code.
   - **UID** — `<docToken>-<backendNodeId>`, valid until the page navigates.
   - **Bounded Capture** — `screencast`: one invocation, no start/stop pair.
   - **The Manual** — `bt guide` / `GUIDE.txt`; `tests/test_guide.py` fails the build when a verb has no entry.
   - **Exit codes** — 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage error. `run` is the one verb printing on stdout at exit 1.
   - **`RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS`** — `{"Page", "Runtime"}`, enabled but never disabled by a step.
   - **Mutation testing** — mutate the *guarantee* (ownership, ordering, timing), not the line just typed.
   - **Model routing** — `choose-model` queried in its own tool block before any delegation; cross-family reviewers use `excludeFamilies: ["claude"]` (family names: claude, glm, meta, openai, qwen — NOT "anthropic").

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`src/browser_tools/step_run.py`** (NEW, the engine). Key structure:
   ```python
   from . import curated, passthrough, step_list
   from .events import WaitTimeout
   from .lifecycle import LifecycleError
   from .one_shot import cli_cdp_errors
   from .passthrough import HiddenTargetError

   STDIN_SOURCE = "-"
   STATUS_OK = "ok"; STATUS_FAILED = "failed"; STATUS_TIMEOUT = "timeout"

   def read_source(source): # StepListError on OSError and UnicodeDecodeError

   @cli_cdp_errors
   def _one_step(step, handler, registry_path):
       from . import cli
       if step.is_passthrough:
           method, params = step.as_method()
           handler.record_caller_enable(method)   # NEWEST addition
           cdp, session_id = handler.require_session()
           try:
               return handler.submit(passthrough.send_on_session(cdp, session_id, method, params))
           except HiddenTargetError as exc:
               raise LifecycleError(str(exc)) from exc
       return cli.step_envelope(step.as_verb(), registry_path, handler=handler)

   def execute(steps, handler, registry_path=None, timeout=None):
       deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout if timeout else None
       handler.set_deadline(deadline)
       entries = []
       try:
           completed, status = _drive(steps, handler, registry_path, timeout, deadline, entries)
       finally:
           handler.set_deadline(None)   # finally: the run does not own this handler
       document = {"run": {"steps": len(steps), "completed": completed, "status": status},
                   "steps": entries}
       return document, status == STATUS_OK

   def _why(exc, timeout): # keeps the step's reason, names the deadline when it caused it

   def _drive(steps, handler, registry_path, timeout, deadline, entries):
       completed = 0
       def overran(): return deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline
       for step in steps:
           if overran():
               return completed, STATUS_TIMEOUT      # no entry for an unstarted step
           entry = {"index": step.number, "step": step.text}
           try:
               result = _one_step(step, handler, registry_path)
           except (TimeoutError, LifecycleError) as exc:
               timed_out = overran() and not isinstance(exc, WaitTimeout)
               status = STATUS_TIMEOUT if timed_out else STATUS_FAILED
               entry["status"] = status
               entry["error"] = _why(exc, timeout if timed_out else None)
               entries.append(entry)
               return completed, status
           entry["result"] = result
           entries.append(entry)
           if overran():
               entry["status"] = STATUS_TIMEOUT
               entry["error"] = f"the run's {timeout}s deadline passed while this step ran"
               return completed, STATUS_TIMEOUT
           entry["status"] = STATUS_OK
           completed += 1
       return completed, STATUS_OK

   def describe_failure(document) -> str | None
   def run(*, instance, source, timeout=None, target=None, url=None, registry_path=None, endpoint=None):
       steps = step_list.validate(read_source(source), registry_path=registry_path, endpoint=endpoint)
       with curated.run_session(instance, target, url, registry_path, endpoint) as handler:
           return execute(steps, handler, registry_path, timeout)
   ```

   **`src/browser_tools/cdp_handler.py`** — many changes:
   ```python
   DEADLINE_GRACE_SECONDS = 5.0
   TEARDOWN_FLOOR_SECONDS = 0.25
   VISIBILITY_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0

   class CDPRuntime:
       _target_by: str | None = None
       _deadline: float | None = None
       _grace_until: float | None = None
       #: Rebound rather than mutated, so the class-level default cannot be
       #: shared by two runtimes built without `__init__`.
       _caller_enabled: frozenset[str] = frozenset()

       def set_deadline(self, deadline): self._deadline = deadline; self._grace_until = None
       @property
       def deadline(self) -> float | None: return self._deadline
       @property
       def caller_enabled(self) -> frozenset[str]: return self._caller_enabled
       def record_caller_enable(self, method: str) -> None:
           domain, _, call = method.partition(".")
           if call == "enable" and domain:
               self._caller_enabled = self._caller_enabled | {domain}

       def bounded_timeout(self, timeout):
           if self._deadline is None: return timeout
           now = time.monotonic()
           remaining = self._deadline - now
           if remaining > 0:
               return remaining if timeout is None else min(timeout, remaining)
           if self._grace_until is None:
               self._grace_until = now + DEADLINE_GRACE_SECONDS
           left = self._grace_until - now
           return max(left, TEARDOWN_FLOOR_SECONDS)
   ```
   `_connect_cdp` was reordered (SUBSCRIBE FIRST): register Page handlers + `Page.navigatedWithinDocument` → `Page.enable` → `Page.getFrameTree` → `update_from_frame_tree` → register Runtime handlers incl. `Runtime.executionContextsCleared` → `Runtime.enable`.

ROOT = Path("/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools/src/browser_tools")

async def domains_enabled(
    cdp: Any, session_id: str, domains: Iterable[str]
) -> AsyncGenerator[None]:'''
new = '''@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def domains_enabled(
    cdp: Any, session_id: str, domains: Iterable[str], keep: Iterable[str] = ()
) -> AsyncGenerator[None]:'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)

old_doc = '''    Two things are deliberately not undone here. Domains in
    :data:`RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS`, per the rule above. And a domain the caller
    enabled by hand in a raw passthrough step, which never reaches this
    function: an enable the caller typed is that step's whole output, and
    undoing it would make the step a no-op. A caller who turns a domain on by
    hand turns it off by hand.
'''
new_doc = '''    Three things are deliberately not undone here. Domains in
    :data:`RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS`, per the rule above. Domains named in ``keep``,
    which are the ones the caller turned on by hand in a raw step: an enable
    the caller typed is that step's whole output, and undoing it would make
    the step a no-op. And a domain whose enable failed, since there is
    nothing to undo.

    ``keep`` exists because CDP cannot answer the question this function
    would otherwise have to ask. A second ``Network.enable`` succeeds exactly
    like a first one, so the reply says nothing about who turned the domain
    on. Without ``keep``, a `network-list` step after a raw `Network.enable`
    step disabled the caller's domain on its way out.

    That makes the two rules collide, and the precedence is stated rather
    than left implicit: **the caller's enable wins**. The cost is that a
    curated step after a hand-written enable does not get a first enable on
    that domain, which is the same exception `Page` and `Runtime` already
    carry. The alternative costs the caller a step that silently did nothing.
'''
assert s.count(old_doc) == 1
s = s.replace(old_doc, new_doc)

old_body = '''    turned_on: list[str] = []
    try:
        for domain in dict.fromkeys(domains):

            except CDPError:
                # No enable for this domain, so nothing to undo either.
                continue
            if domain not in RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS:
                turned_on.append(domain)
        yield'''
new_body = '''    mine_to_undo = RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS | frozenset(keep)
    turned_on: list[str] = []
    try:
        for domain in dict.fromkeys(domains):
            try:

            except CDPError:
                # No enable for this domain, so nothing to undo either.
                continue
            if domain not in mine_to_undo:
                turned_on.append(domain)
        yield'''

s = p.read_text()
old_l = "        async with domains_enabled(cdp, session_id, (e.split(\".\")[0] for e in events)):"
new_l = "        async with domains_enabled(cdp, session_id, (e.split(\".\")[0] for e in events), keep):"

            parent = self._frames.get(frame.parent_frame_id)
            if parent:
                parent.children = [c for c in parent.children if c.frame_id != frame_id]

        if self._selected_frame_id == frame_id:

new_detach = '''        # Detaching a frame destroys everything inside it. Removing only this
        # frame leaves its children in the map with a `parent_frame_id` that
        # no longer resolves, which cuts them out of the tree and out of
        # `_forget_descendants`, so a later navigation cannot remove them
        # either. They stay selectable, because `_resolve_frame_by_url` walks
        # the map rather than the tree.
        self._forget_descendants(frame_id)

        if frame and frame.parent_frame_id:
            parent = self._frames.get(frame.parent_frame_id)
            if parent:
                parent.children = [c for c in parent.children if c.frame_id != frame_id]

        # Clear selection if detached frame was selected. The pattern is kept,
        # so a later navigation that brings a matching frame back re-points at
        # it; only `frames reset` and a new `frames select` clear the pattern.
        if self._selected_frame_id == frame_id:

            # it a re-resolution that finds nothing leaves the previous frame id
            # in place, and the next frame-scoped read succeeds against a frame
            # whose URL no longer matches the pattern the caller selected. Inside

new_block = '''    def _reresolve_selection(self) -> None:
        """Re-point the selection at whatever now matches its pattern.

        The `else` matters (RFC-03, "Frame selection across steps"). Without
        it a re-resolution that finds nothing leaves the previous frame id in
        place, and the next frame-scoped read succeeds against a frame whose
        URL no longer matches the pattern the caller selected. Inside a Step
        Run the selection outlives the step, so that stale id is read by later
        steps.

        The pattern is kept, matching what a detach does. A later navigation
        that brings a matching frame back re-points the selection at it.
        """
        if not self._selected_url_pattern:
            return
        resolved = self._resolve_frame_by_url(self._selected_url_pattern)
        self._selected_frame_id = resolved.frame_id if resolved else None

    def handle_navigated_within_document(self, params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Handle Page.navigatedWithinDocument, a History API route change.

        A single-page app changes its URL through `history.pushState` rather
        than by loading a document, and Chrome reports that with its own
        event. Handling only `Page.frameNavigated` meant the frame kept the
        URL it was first loaded with: `frames list` reported the old route,
        and a selection made by pattern went on matching a URL the page had
        left. The Shopify admin and most consoles are single-page apps, so
        this is the common case rather than the exotic one.

        The document is the same one, so its child frames survive and nothing
        is forgotten here. Only the URL changed, so only the selection is
        re-resolved against it.
        """
        frame_id = params.get("frameId", "")
        url = params.get("url")
        if not frame_id or url is None:
            return

        frame = self._frames.get(frame_id)
        if frame is None:
            return
        frame.url = url

        self._reresolve_selection()
        self._event_buffer.append(
            FrameEvent(event_type="navigated", frame_id=frame_id, url=url)
        )

    def handle_execution_contexts_cleared(self, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
        """Handle Runtime.executionContextsCleared.

        Every context the page had is gone. Keeping the map would leave each
        frame holding a destroyed context id, which a frame-scoped read then
        evaluates against and gets an error for, or worse, silently skips.
        """
        self._execution_contexts.clear()
        for frame in self._frames.values():
            frame.execution_context_id = None

    def _forget_descendants(self, frame_id: str) -> None:'''

s = s.replace(old_anchor, new_block)

p.write_text(s)

**Blocking findings remain.** The new disable refusal held under the spellings I tested. The remaining problems concern domain ownership, frame state, and the navigation advice.

This was a controlled-transport review. Connecting to `127.0.0.1:9222` raised `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. I could not run live checks or measure CDP latency.

**Blocking**

1. **A curated step disables a domain enabled by a raw step.**

   [one_shot.py:98](/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools/src/browser_tools/one_shot.py:98) records every successful enable as its own. It cannot distinguish a fresh enable from a redundant enable.

   Reproduction: raw `Network.enable`, then `network-list --duration 0`. The controlled transport recorded:

   ```text
   ['Network.enable', 'Network.enable', 'Network.disable']
   ```

   Rule 3 requires the caller’s enable to survive. The helper instead disables it. This also contradicts the manual’s ownership paragraph.

   Rules 1 and 3 need an explicit precedence rule: preserving a caller-owned enable necessarily means the next curated step cannot receive a first enable.

2. **The run loses the initial execution-context replay.**

   [cdp_handler.py:624](/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools/src/browser_tools/cdp_handler.py:624) enables Runtime before registering its context handlers. It also constructs the initial frame tree after that enable.

   Delivering `Runtime.executionContextCreated` during enable produces:

   ```text
   initial context: None
   storage: Cookies (0):
   ```

   The storage step succeeds while omitting localStorage and sessionStorage. Runtime’s immediate replay is documented behavior, not an invented transport condition. [Runtime protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/js_protocol.pdl)

   This predates the reviewed commits, but it breaks the landed frame-scoped storage contract.

3. **Same-document navigation leaves the old URL and selection intact.**

   The runtime does not subscribe to `Page.navigatedWithinDocument`. Delivering that event with a new URL of `/done` leaves the selected frame reporting:

   ```text
   after same-document navigation: https://x.test/checkout
   ```

   Rule 5 requires the selection to clear when its pattern stops matching. History API navigation has a dedicated CDP event, so handling only `frameNavigated` does not cover it. [Page protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/domains/Page.pdl)

   This is another existing gap exposed by the new contract.

4. **A parent detach can leave a selectable orphan that later navigation cannot remove.**

   Starting with `R → P → C`, select C, detach P, then navigate R. Result:

   ```text
   after detach and navigation: ['R'] C
   ```

   The list contains only R, but C remains selected. [handle_frame_detached](/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools/src/browser_tools/frame_manager.py:296) removes only P. That severs the parent chain `_forget_descendants` needs to find C.

   This violates rules 5 and 6 under the supplied event sequence. I reproduced the invariant failure directly; I did not establish this event ordering against live Chrome.

5. **The new post-navigation wait advice can time out after navigation has finished.**

   Deliver `Page.loadEventFired` before the next step registers its handler, then execute the recommended wait:

   ```text
   load already delivered: WaitTimeout
   ```

   `wait` buffers events only after subscription. Keeping Page enabled does not retain earlier load events.

   `wait-idle` avoids that particular subscription race, but its implementation polls completed resource entries. It does not explicitly synchronize with the navigation’s loader or the frame manager. The manual should not present either command as an unconditional navigation barrier.

The following command reproduces those five findings without sockets or filesystem writes. Run location: `/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools`.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -B -c '
import asyncio,runpy
from browser_tools import list_verbs,events
from browser_tools.cdp_handler import CDPHandler
from browser_tools.frame_manager import FrameManager
FakeCDP=runpy.run_path("tests/test_session_hygiene.py")["FakeCDP"]

class Wire(FakeCDP):
 _connected=True
 def emit(self,event,params):
  for callback in self.handlers.get(event,[]): callback(params)
 async def send(self,method,params=None,session_id=None,**kw):
  await super().send(method,params,session_id)
  if method=="Runtime.enable":
   self.emit("Runtime.executionContextCreated",{"context":{"id":7,"auxData":{"frameId":"R","isDefault":True}}})
  if method=="Page.getFrameTree":
   return {"frameTree":{"frame":{"id":"R","url":"https://x.test/checkout"}}}
  return {}

class Stack:
 def __init__(self,c): self.c=c
 async def enter_async_context(self,cm): return self.c,"S1"

async def probe():
 c=FakeCDP()
 await c.send("Network.enable",session_id="S1")
 await list_verbs.collect_on_session(c,"S1",list_verbs.NETWORK_EVENTS,0)
 print("raw domain:",c.calls)

 h._rt._sessions=Stack(c);h._rt._frame_manager=FrameManager()
 await h._rt._connect_cdp()
 m=h._rt._frame_manager;m.select_frame_by_url("checkout")
 print("initial context:",m.get_selected_execution_context_id())
 print("storage:",(await h._handle_get_frame_storage({}))["result"]["content"][0]["text"])

 c.emit("Page.navigatedWithinDocument",{"frameId":"R","url":"https://x.test/done","navigationType":"historyApi"})
 print("after same-document navigation:",m.get_selected_frame().url)

 c.emit("Runtime.executionContextCreated",{"context":{"id":8,"auxData":{"frameId":"R","isDefault":True}}})
 c.emit("Runtime.executionContextsCleared",{})
 print("after contexts cleared:",m.get_selected_execution_context_id())

 c.emit("Page.loadEventFired",{"timestamp":1})
 try:
  await events.wait_on_session(c,"S1","Page.loadEventFired",None,0.001)
 except events.WaitTimeout:
  print("load already delivered: WaitTimeout")

asyncio.run(probe())

m.update_from_frame_tree({"frame":{"id":"R","url":"root"},"childFrames":[{"frame":{"id":"P","url":"parent"},"childFrames":[{"frame":{"id":"C","url":"checkout"}}]}]})
m.select_frame_by_url("checkout")
m.handle_frame_detached({"frameId":"P","reason":"remove"})
m.handle_frame_navigated({"frame":{"id":"R","url":"done"}})

**Non-blocking findings and qualifications**

- **Another stale representation is the execution-context map.** The reproducer prints `after contexts cleared: 8`. The runtime ignores `Runtime.executionContextsCleared`; the frame retains a destroyed context ID. This needs a live navigation regression test before assigning its end-to-end severity.

- **Rule 5 itself is too narrow.** `storage get --key account` changes the persistent selection pattern too. I ran `curated.frames_select(...pattern="checkout")`, followed by `curated.storage_get(...key="account")` through the actual handlers. The resulting pattern was `account`. The manual’s sentence limiting pattern changes to `frames reset` and `frames select` is false. [curated.py:548](/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools/src/browser_tools/curated.py:548)

- **CONTEXT.md overstates comment syntax.** With the registry mocked empty, `step_list.validate("Page.getFrameTree # comment")` raises:

  ```text
  line 1: 'Page.getFrameTree' takes at most one JSON params argument
  ```

  Only whole comment lines are ignored. `#` does not generally start a comment as the glossary says.

- **Cleanup is best-effort, not unconditional.** A third enable raising `ValueError` correctly unwound the first two domains:

  ```text
  Network.enable, Log.enable, DOM.enable, Log.disable, Network.disable
  ```

  Ordinary cancellation during the body also attempted both disables. But a second cancellation during `Log.disable` stopped cleanup before `Network.disable`. Likewise, an injected `TimeoutError` during disable replaced the body’s `ValueError` and skipped remaining cleanup. The current raw client normally surfaces protocol and connection errors, which are suppressed. I have not established a production path for that injected timeout.

**The refusal and termination checks**

I found no spelling bypass for `Page.disable` or `Runtime.disable`. Quoted and backslash spellings that normalize to those methods are refused. Case changes and trailing characters pass validation but are transmitted unchanged; the code does not normalize them into forbidden methods afterward.

I would retain the Runtime refusal. Disabling its context notifications defeats context tracking. A caller may reasonably want to suppress notifications, but the current Step Run cannot support that while promising frame-scoped reads.

`Target.detachFromTarget` is accepted by validation, but acceptance alone is not a reproduced vulnerability. Current Chromium looks up the supplied identifier in the receiving handler’s attached child sessions; an empty request fails, and the session carrying the request is not an implicit self-detach target. This is a source-based assessment, not an installed-browser result. I did not establish another raw-method bypass. [Chromium Target handler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/content/browser/devtools/protocol/target_handler.cc)

`_forget_descendants` terminates for every finite, stable frame map, including cycles. Each candidate enters `doomed` before entering `frontier`, and can enter only once. With N entries, there are at most N+1 frontier removals. I also exercised all 700 parent graphs with one through four nodes. Every call terminated. Cycles can cause the starting frame to be removed, but cannot make this loop infinite.

**Mutation results**

All 12 original mutations were caught when applied in memory.

These additional mutations each returned `34 passed, 1 deselected`:

| Mutation | Coverage gap |
|---|---|
| Move enables outside the cleanup `try` | No partial-enable failure test |
| Send enable/disable without `session_id` | FakeCDP ignores session identity |
| Skip Runtime enable in collections | Console test checks cleanup, not successful subscription setup |
| Swallow every ordinary enable exception | No test requiring non-CDP enable failures to propagate |
| Remove the navigating frame too | Tests miss divergence between stored child objects and the map |
| Remove eager selection clearing during pruning | Equivalent for the reachable nonempty-pattern path |

In particular, `test_two_collections_in_one_session_each_get_a_first_enable` survives sending every domain command to the wrong session. It checks method names, not first-enable behavior.

The first dropped mutation is **not equivalent**. I changed `doomed` to start with `[frame_id]`, navigated an existing child, and compared tree and flat views:

```text
baseline tree/flat: ('new', 'new')
dropped mutant tree/flat: ('old', 'new')
```

Recreating the child replaces the map entry but leaves its parent holding the old `FrameInfo`. All current hygiene tests still passed. The second dropped mutation is equivalent for the CLI’s nonempty selection patterns because the subsequent re-resolution clears the ID.

**Validation limits**

This command passed:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --noconftest -q -s -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/test_frame_manager.py tests/test_session_hygiene.py \
  -k 'not nothing_runs'
```

Result: **59 passed, 1 deselected**. Normal fixture setup failed because the sandbox cannot create temporary directories. The excluded test writes a Step List file.

No latency measurement was possible, so the approximately 1 ms claim remains unverified here. The existing live network-list checks also do not distinguish fresh-enable behavior from an already-enabled domain receiving fresh traffic.

I changed no files. During review, HEAD advanced to `8f5cf66`, adding guide tests; the reviewed production files stayed unchanged. An independently modified `tests/test_step_run.py` was left untouched.

# Adversarial review: session hygiene and the landed contract (RFC-03 Phases 4 and 5)

Repository: `/Users/kevin/dev/browser-tools`. Branch: `feat/session-hygiene`.
Two commits: `faab7af` (behaviour) and `a9a3836` (docs).
Diff them with `git diff 0f9a98f..HEAD`.

You have read and write access. Run things. Break things. Restore what you break.

**Your sandbox may refuse sockets.** The last review of this work could not
reach `127.0.0.1:9222` and said so, which was the right call. If yours cannot
either, say so plainly and review what you can reach. Do not report a
controlled-transport result as a live one.

## What the product is

`bt` is a Python CLI that drives Chrome over CDP. `bt run FILE` (RFC-03,
landed in #131) runs an ordered list of steps against one browser, in one
invocation, over one CDP connection.

Read `docs/rfc/03_*.rfc.md`, sections "Domain-enable state, and why it needs a
rule" and "Frame selection across steps". `CONTEXT.md` is the naming
authority. `src/browser_tools/GUIDE.txt` is the shipped manual.

## The problem this solves

A one-shot invocation could leave the session in any state, because the
session was detached moments later. A run's session outlives every step, so
whatever step 3 leaves on is still on at step 9.

## What changed

- `src/browser_tools/one_shot.py`: `domains_enabled`, an async context
  manager that enables domains for the body and disables on the way out, and
  `RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS = {"Page", "Runtime"}`, which are enabled but never
  disabled.
- `src/browser_tools/events.py`, `list_verbs.py`: both now go through it.
- `src/browser_tools/frame_manager.py`: two fixes. Re-resolution after a
  navigation now clears the selected frame id on a no-match instead of
  leaving the previous one. And `_forget_descendants` drops the old
  document's child frames when a frame navigates.
- `src/browser_tools/cdp_handler.py`: the "No frame selected" diagnostic no
  longer claims a selection cannot carry over, which is false inside a run.
- `GUIDE.txt`, `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/rfc/01_*.rfc.md`: the contract.
- `tests/test_session_hygiene.py` is new (27 tests).

## The rules, stated so you can attack them

1. **A step gives back every domain it turned on**, so the next step wanting
   that domain still gets a *first* enable. A first `Runtime.enable` replays
   the contexts that already exist; a second replays nothing. The RFC measured
   it: 2 events, then 0, then 2 on a fresh session.
2. **Except `Page` and `Runtime`**, which the run needs on throughout to track
   frames. A step that disabled `Page` would break frame selection for every
   later step.
3. **A domain the caller enabled by hand in a raw step is not undone.** That
   enable is the step's whole output.
4. **A disable that fails must not fail the step**, and must not mask what the
   step body raised.
5. **A frame selection follows its pattern across a navigation**, and is
   cleared when the pattern no longer matches. The pattern itself survives, so
   a matching frame coming back re-selects it. Only `frames reset` and a new
   `frames select` clear the pattern.
6. **A navigated frame forgets its descendants.** Chrome sends no
   `Page.frameDetached` for them.

## What I already did

- 1357 tests, `ruff check src/ tests/`, `pyright src/`, all clean.
- 12 mutations against rules 1 to 6, all caught:
  `.scratch/rfc-03-phase4/mutate_hygiene.py`. It restores every file it edits
  and bounds each run at 300s.
- A live harness against headless Chrome, green:
  `.scratch/rfc-03-phase4/live_hygiene.sh`, transcript in `live_hygiene.txt`.
- The `frameDetached` claim in rule 6 is measured, not assumed: I ran
  `bt attach +Page.frameDetached +Page.frameNavigated` across a navigation and
  only `frameNavigated` arrived.

Two mutations I dropped as equivalent rather than as surviving, with reasons
in the harness file. Check my reasoning on both; if either is a real hole, say
so.

## What I want from you

1. **Ordering and failure in `domains_enabled`.** The enable loop is inside
   the `try`, so a failure partway through still disables what it got to. Is
   that right? If the enable of domain 3 raises something that is not
   `CDPError`, what happens to domains 1 and 2? Is the `finally` reachable in
   every path, including cancellation?
2. **The exemption.** `RUN_OWNED_DOMAINS` is checked when recording what to
   undo, not when enabling. Convince yourself a step cannot disable `Page` by
   any route: a raw step can send `Page.disable` directly, and the RFC says
   that is the caller's business. Is it? A raw `Page.disable` step would break
   frame selection for every later step in the run. I think the RFC is wrong
   here and this should be refused at validation. Argue it either way.
3. **`_forget_descendants`.** It walks `self._frames` by parent id, inside a
   `while frontier` loop. Prove it terminates on every input, including a
   cycle in `parent_frame_id` (which a hostile or buggy browser could
   produce). I hung my own mutation harness for 12 minutes with a mutant that
   looped here, so the shape is not obviously safe.
4. **What else holds a stale frame.** `_frames` is one map; `children` lists
   are another representation. After a navigation, can the two disagree? Is
   there any path that leaves a frame in one and not the other? An orphan in
   `_frames` is selectable, because `_resolve_frame_by_url` walks that map
   rather than the tree. That is exactly the bug I fixed, so I want the
   remaining paths checked.
5. **The cost.** One extra round trip per domain per step. Measure it if you
   can reach a browser. The RFC budgeted about 1 ms against the 85 ms a step
   saves. Is that what it actually costs?
6. **The contract.** Read `GUIDE.txt`'s `RUNNING MANY STEPS` section and
   `CONTEXT.md`'s new nouns against what the code does. Find a sentence that
   is not true. I added one paragraph the RFC does not contain, about waiting
   after a navigation before reading; check it is accurate.
7. **Tests that pass against broken code.** Mutate the rules, not the lines.
   Tell me which of my 27 tests survive a mutation they claim to cover.

## Rules

- Do not fix anything. Report.
- A finding needs a reproduction: the command, the output, and what the rule
  above says should have happened instead.
- Separate **blocking** from **non-blocking**.
- If a rule in this brief is itself wrong, say so. Item 2 is the one I most
  suspect.
- Voice: plain, no em dashes, no praise.

## Output

Return your report as your final message. The last reviewer's sandbox was
read-only and could not write a file, so do not depend on writing one.

## Addendum: item 2 turned out to be a real hole, and is now fixed

I tested it before sending this. Commit `a9bb580`.

With `Page.disable '{}'` as step 2 of a run: step 3 navigated to a page with
no iframe, step 5 `frames list` reported the page the run had left, step 6
`storage get` read a frame that no longer existed and succeeded, and the run
exited 0. Silent corruption of every step after the disable.

`Page.disable` and `Runtime.disable` are now refused at validation, exit 2,
nothing sent. `Page.enable` and `Runtime.enable` by hand are still allowed.

So do not re-find that one. Attack the fix instead:

- Is the refusal reachable around? The check is on `method.partition(".")` in
  `_validate_passthrough`. Is there a spelling of `Page.disable` that a step
  can carry and this check does not see?
- Are there other CDP methods a raw step can send that break the run's own
  state the same way, silently? `Target.detachFromTarget` on the run's own
  session is the one I would look at next, and I have not checked it.
- Is refusing `Runtime.disable` over-refusing? I could not construct a case
  where a caller wants it inside a run, but I did not try hard.

The brief's rule list above now has a seventh rule: **a step must not disable
`Page` or `Runtime`.**

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kevin/.claude/skills/choose-model

# Choose Model

Model routing is a lookup, not a judgment call. One command over
`references/registry.json` answers "which model, and which ones after
it" the same way every time. The unit it ranks is a **route**: a model
reached through one harness. The same model through two harnesses is
two routes, and they sit next to each other in the answer.

## When to query

Before any delegation where the model is not already pinned by the user
or by the calling skill's own spec: a subagent, a worker on another
harness, a reviewer (cross-family or not), a workflow stage, or the
question "which model should do X".

Skip it when a model is pinned, or when the work is a single edit
cheaper to make than to describe.

## The command

```bash
npx tsx <skill-dir>/scripts/choose.ts '<query-json>'   # or pipe JSON on stdin
npx tsx <skill-dir>/scripts/choose.ts --tasks          # task types
npx tsx <skill-dir>/scripts/choose.ts --models         # model and route facts
npx tsx <skill-dir>/scripts/choose.ts --matrix         # tables, for a human
```

`<skill-dir>` is the directory containing this loaded `SKILL.md`.
`--matrix` is for reading and for
explaining a decision after the fact. Never pick a model by reading the
matrix; that is the judgment call the query exists to replace.

## Query

```json
{ "task": "code-review", "stakes": "normal", "privacy": "normal",
  "needs": ["skills"], "excludeFamilies": ["glm"] }
```

- `task` (required): a registry task type; `--tasks` lists them.
- `stakes`: `low` | `normal` | `high` (default `normal`). Picks the
  minimums row. Low is throwaway; high is architecture-level or a
  user-facing hot path.
- `privacy`: `normal` | `secret` (default `normal`). `secret` means the
  prompt would carry secret material (credentials, tokens, `.env`
  contents, production output). Hosted routes are excluded outright.
- `needs`: extra capabilities beyond the task's own, e.g. `browser`,
  `desktop`, `skills`.
- `prefer`: `cost` | `speed` (default `cost`). `speed` ranks the routes
  that clear the minimums by measured response time, fastest first, with
  unmeasured routes last. Use it for quick lookups and exploration where
  waiting costs more than the call.
- `excludeFamilies`: hard exclusions. Pass the implementer's family when
  picking a reviewer so a model never reviews its own work.

## Building the query from a description

Writing `task` by hand is the judgment the registry exists to replace, and
`--tasks` is a list of eleven. When you have prose and not a query, build it:

```bash
npx tsx <skill-dir>/scripts/routing-query.ts --description <file> \
  [--stakes high] [--privacy secret] [--task implement] [--needs skills]
```

Out comes `query` (feed it straight to `choose.ts`) and `report`.

It asks four questions in one request and **decides only two fields**:

- **`task`**, when it is at least 0.85 confident. Below that the answer is
  still returned and `report.taskSource` says `jev-low-confidence`: supply
  `--task` yourself, or unattended take it and record that you did.
- **`needs`**, escalate-only. A high answer adds `browser` or `desktop`. A
  low one never removes a capability you asked for, because you know things
  the description does not carry.

**`stakes` and `privacy` are yours, always.** `stakes` is not asked at all;
it measured 58% and its confidence did not track its accuracy. `privacy` is
asked, recorded in `report.carriesSecret`, and gates nothing: three labelled
positives cannot set a threshold on a failure that leaks a credential. Set
`--privacy secret` yourself whenever the rule in GLOBAL.md applies.

The work description is the whole state, so its shape decides the answer.
Four rules govern it, and they were measured: applied to the five
descriptions the task question got wrong, the originals scored 0 of 5 and the
rewrites 4 of 5. Read
[references/work-description.md](references/work-description.md) before
writing one.

They fix the answer, not the confidence. Most recovered rows stay below the
act-band, so the caller still confirms the task. Shape rules do not buy
autonomy.

### When Jev does not answer

Routing keeps working. Only `MISSING_KEY` is fatal, because it is a setup
error and the message already names the wrapper that supplies the key.

Every other failure falls back to a **registry-chosen local route** that
decides `task` and the capability flags, and nothing else. `privacy` and
`stakes` take their safe values, `secret` and `high`, unless you stated them
yourself. The errors are asymmetric: a wrong `privacy` leaks a credential, a
wrong `task` wastes a run. The local route is never asked about privacy, so
there is no answer to be tempted by, and no uncalibrated number to mistake
for a band tuned on Jev's.

`report.fallback` records the code and the route, so an outage is visible in
the record instead of looking like a normal answer.

Two consequences to expect:

- **The query lands in the shortfall warning** for any task whose floor the
  local fleet cannot reach, because `privacy` is `secret`. That warning is
  written to read correctly here, where the cause is an outage rather than
  secret material.
- **There are no pane answers.** Give the worker a shell and treat the size
  as unknown.

## Output

**Artifact:** a route-choice JSON object on stdout. **Contains:** the selected
route, ordered fallbacks, exclusions and warnings described below. **Not:**
a worker execution, a reachability check, or a registry edit.

`selection` is the route to try first. `fallbacks` are every other
route that survived the hard constraints, best first. `excluded` gives
each dropped route with its reason. `warnings` says when nothing met the
bar and the most capable survivor was returned instead.

In practice that warning means one thing. Over all 264 reachable queries,
26 warn and **every one is `privacy: secret`**: the routes that could
clear a high floor are all privacy-ineligible, so the warning is not a
borderline model, it is secret work meeting a floor the local fleet
cannot reach. Two options, and the warning says both: run the local route
and verify its output harder, or do not do this work on this machine.
**Relaxing the query is not an option.** Privacy work never reroutes to a
hosted model, even when no local model is reachable.

The same branch catches an outage, because routing that cannot reach Jev
falls back with `privacy` at its safe value. Same symptom, different
cause, same answer.

Each route carries `route` (`<model>@<harness>`, the label a delegation
reports), `harness`, `modelId` (the id `hcn run --model` takes),
`provider` (pi only, else null), `effort`, `responseSeconds` (null when
unmeasured), the model's scores, `score`
and `scoredBy` (the figure checked against the intelligence minimum, and
whether it came from `intelligence` or the task's facet), and `notes`
with the route's operational traps.

Errors exit 1 with a JSON `error` object: `UNKNOWN_TASK`,
`UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY`, `UNKNOWN_FAMILY`, `BAD_INPUT`, `BAD_JSON`,
`NO_CANDIDATES`, `BAD_REGISTRY`, and `PRIVACY_UNSATISFIABLE`, which
means the work runs locally or not at all, never on a hosted model.

## How selection works

1. Hard filters drop routes and record why: privacy, excluded families,
   missing capabilities (task `requires` plus query `needs`).
2. The task's minimums at the given stakes (intelligence and taste
   floors, model-level) split survivors into passing and failing. A task
   that names a facet checks the model's facet score against the
   intelligence floor instead; a model with no score for it uses
   intelligence.
3. Cheapest passing route wins (cost is cheapness), or the fastest under
   `prefer: "speed"`. Ties break by that score, then taste, then the
   model's own route order. Cost order is the escalation ladder as data:
   local, then the price-ranked hosted routes, then Claude.
4. Nothing passing: the most capable survivor, with a warning.
5. Effort is resolved last: the model's `fixedReasoning` if it has one,
   else the task's reasoning clamped by the model's `maxReasoning`.

## What it does not do

<!-- skill-graph: mentions - names the owner of the walk; this skill never
     invokes delegate -->

It does not run anything, probe whether a harness is installed or
authenticated, or walk failures. Whether a route is reachable right now
is learned from hcn's typed failure when the delegation runs; the
[delegate](../delegate/SKILL.md) skill owns that walk. Registry edits,
scoring, and the effort ceiling are in
[references/REGISTRY.md](references/REGISTRY.md); edit the registry,
never the script, to change routing.


ARGUMENTS: Adversarial code review of a new CLI execution engine (Python, ~180 lines of new module plus wiring) that runs an ordered list of steps over one shared CDP browser session. Needs a reader who will hunt for ownership, ordering, and timing defects, run mutations against the test suite, and drive a real browser. Implementer family: anthropic. Need excludeFamilies: anthropic. Read-and-write access (it should be able to run the suite and probe). Task type: code review.
